articles.title: Seahawks Drop Unfortunate Zach Charbonnet News
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks may have to wait beyond Thursday for the backfield reinforcement they badly need.Head coach Mike Macdonald indicated after Sunday’s 32-2...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks may have to wait beyond Thursday for the backfield reinforcement they badly need.

Head coach Mike Macdonald indicated after Sunday's 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers that running back Zach Charbonnet is not expected to return for Thursday night's road matchup with the Denver Broncos.

Corbin K. Smith reported on X that Macdonald said the current plan is for Charbonnet not to play against Denver. Seattle's official team site later confirmed the update, with Macdonald leaving only a small opening for the plan to change.

The timing makes the development sting even more. Seattle committed four turnovers against San Francisco, and two came from running backs Emanuel Wilson and George Holani . The 49ers converted the Seahawks' mistakes into 21 points in a three-point game.

Macdonald Pumps Brakes on Charbonnet Return

Charbonnet has been working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in Seattle's divisional-round win over San Francisco in January. The Seahawks placed him on the physically unable to perform list to begin the season before designating him to return to practice on Oct. 1.

That move opened a 21-day practice window for Seattle to activate Charbonnet to the 53-man roster. Macdonald had already pointed to the short Denver week as a complication because the Seahawks would have fewer full-speed practice opportunities.

Following Sunday's loss, Macdonald made the outlook clearer.

"That could change, but as of right now, he's not going to play," Macdonald said , per Seahawks.com.

The short turnaround gives Seattle only four days between the loss to the 49ers and its Week 6 trip to Denver. Charbonnet has practiced for two weeks, but the Seahawks have continued to take a cautious approach with a player returning from major knee surgery.

If he remains sidelined, Seattle is expected to lean again on Wilson, Holani and Velus Jones Jr.. Newcomer Robert Henry Jr. could also be an option after being inactive against San Francisco.

Seahawks Need Charbonnet After Costly 49ers Fumbles

Sunday showed why Charbonnet's return has become so important.

Wilson was stripped by Fred Warner deep in Seattle territory in the second quarter, setting up an 11-yard Christian McCaffrey touchdown on the next snap. Later, Holani fumbled at his own goal line with 13 seconds left in the half, allowing 49ers defensive lineman Gracen Halton to recover in the end zone.

Holani actually fumbled twice in the first half, though the Seahawks recovered the first one. Wilson finished with 61 rushing yards and a touchdown on 20 carries, but his lost fumble helped turn a promising afternoon into another turnover-heavy loss

Charbonnet would bring a different track record. Via NFL.com , he rushed for 730 yards and 12 touchdowns on 184 carries last season and did not fumble once. Across his first three NFL seasons, he has 1,761 rushing yards, 21 touchdowns and zero recorded fumbles.

That ball security stands out after what happened Sunday, when Seattle's available backs put the ball on the ground three times between them.

The Seahawks can't rush Charbonnet back simply because the current backfield struggled, especially coming off an ACL tear.

But due to another costly day from the available runners, the plan to keep him out Thursday leaves Seattle with the same group for a potentially grinding road game in Denver.

articles.title: Mark Andrews struggles on Sunday Night Football
articles.summary: Mark Andrews caught four passes for just 28 yards on Sunday night and had a fumble returned for a score by the Atlanta Falcons defense.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens TE Mark Andrews was targeted six times against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, resulting in four catches for 28 yards. Andrews also lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown.

Why It Matters: Make it three straight weeks under 30 yards receiving for Andrews, who looks almost exactly like the player that put up a 48-422-5 line a season ago. Any hope that the 31-year-old would enjoy a career renaissance, at least to the 2024 version that scored 11 touchdowns, seems to fade week by week. In deeper leagues he can be carried as a low-end TE2 as he's been targeted at least five times in each game, but those in standard formats shouldn't go out of their way to carry Andrews on their roster.

articles.title: Teenage archer aiming for Youth Olympics glory
articles.summary: Archie Christopher, from Solihull, will represent Team GB at the Youth Olympics in Senegal.
articles.body:
A teenage archer who only took up the sport four years ago, is to represent Great Britain in the Youth Olympics.

Archie Christopher, from Solihull, will take part in the competition in Senegal, starting at the end of October.

The 17-year-old, who trains at the Meriden Archery Club, only made his international debut earlier this year, but will make history when he and the rest of Team GB take part in the first Olympic event to be held on African soil.

"Its a shock that I'm going to an event such as this, considering I've only made my debut this year", he said.

Archery is one of the world's oldest sports still played today, with historical records showing it was considered a sport by the Egyptian Pharaohs in the 15th century BCE.

The competition at the Youth Olympics will start on 6 November at the Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio, around 30km (18 miles) from the capital, Dakar.

Christopher said being part of the team to take part in the first-ever Olympic event held in Africa was special.

When asked about being told he had been selected for the Great Britain team, he said: "I was speechless really. I don't know how to describe it. There's no real words".

At 17, Christopher is one of the older members of the Team GB contingent heading to West Africa, and one of just two archers.

The teenager is currently studying for a BTEC in engineering, but is not sure what he wants to do after the course ends.

His father, Paul, said he actually found out before his son that he had made Team GB.

"I couldn't believe what I was reading and had to read it three times to make sure it was saying he'd been selected.

"I immediately forwarded the email to Archie and his mum because I was at work at the time and then phoned them up and we were all in bits."

However, even though his son is taking part in a history-making Youth Olympics, he said he will have to watch his son shoot on the TV.

"We have a younger son who going to be in school and can't really afford to take him out of school."

"We'll be watching and rooting for him from home."

articles.title: Falcons blow 4th quarter lead, lose to Ravens in overtime
articles.summary: Tyler Huntley led Baltimore to a tying touchdown and 2-point conversion in the last minute of regulation and then scored on a 1-yard sneak in overtime as the...
articles.body:
With Tyler Huntley filling in at quarterback, the Baltimore Ravens were on Snoop patrol.

When "Snoop" Huntley is leading the offense, the Ravens don't feel like a backup is on the field.

Huntley led Baltimore to a tying touchdown and 2-point conversion in the last minute of regulation and then scored on a 1-yard sneak in overtime as the Ravens rallied to beat the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 on Sunday night.

"There's not a locker room in the NFL that has my confidence in their backup quarterback than we have in Snoop," coach Jesse Minter said.

Added safety Kyle Hamilton, whose interception in overtime ended the game: "When Snoop gets a chance to go out there, it's a Snoop game. It's not a backup quarterback, and he's done it so any times. It's a blessing to have him."

Derrick Henry ran for 102 yards against the Falcons' top-ranked run defense for the Ravens (4-1).

"If we let it be, this can be a launching point for us to really get this thing rolling," said Minter after the Ravens took sole possession of first place in the AFC North.

After Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury late in the fourth quarter, Tua Tagovailoa took over at quarterback for the Falcons (2-3) in overtime. Tagovailoa's pass for Drake London was intercepted by Hamilton to end the game.

"We didn't do enough to win the game," Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said.

Huntley completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards and two touchdowns as the fill-in starter for Lamar Jackson , who has an ankle injury and cheered from the sideline in street clothes.

Penix overcame a slow start to pass for 240 yards and a touchdown but could only watch from the bench with a towel on his head as the Ravens put the game away.

Jessie Bates III returned a recovered fumble 36 yards for a score for Atlanta in the first quarter.

Bijan Robinson ran for 86 yards, but Penix's 5-yard scoring pass to Kyle Pitts was Atlanta's only offensive touchdown.

With Baltimore trailing 23-15, Huntley threw a 7-yard scoring pass to Devontez Walker with 40 seconds remaining in regulation and Henry took the direct snap and ran left for the tying conversion. Huntley targeted Falcons backup cornerback Mike Ford for the touchdown pass a play after Mike Hughes left the game with an injury.

After Huntley's third-down pass to tight end Mark Andrews was broken up by a big hit from Falcons safety Xavier Watts with 6:28 remaining, the Ravens were forced to punt.

Hamilton grew up in Atlanta and attended Marist School. There was a strong showing from Ravens fans at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and many were there to cheer for Hamilton.

"I probably know 500 people or something in the stadium right now," Hamilton said. "It was a pretty special moment."

Huntley scored on a second-down run from the 1 to give Baltimore the lead late in regulation.

"I was just doing my job," Huntley said. "Once you get in the end zone you give off an "Ah!" and I was ready to get on the sideline and cheer our defense on."

Penix finds his form to help Falcons build first-half lead

Bates' return for a first-quarter touchdown gave Atlanta the early lead. Safety Sydney Brown forced the fumble by Andrews.

Penix was a combined 0-for-4 passing on Atlanta's first three possessions before finally reclaiming the form he showed while leading the Falcons to back-to-back wins. A screen pass to Pitts seemed to spark Penix, who was 5-for-5 on a touchdown drive that included a 25-yard completion to London and a 36-yard pass to Jahan Dotson to the Ravens 6.

Penix found Pitts again over the middle for a 5-yard touchdown pass.

The Ravens were more effective than the Falcons in moving the ball most of the first half but had to settle for Tyler Loop's field goals of 21, 51 and 51 yards as Atlanta led 14-9 at halftime.

Baltimore opened the second half with a drive built around a 47-yard run by Justice Hill. Huntley's 18-yard scoring pass to Henry cut the Falcons' lead to 17-15 when the 2-point pass to Andrews was incomplete.

Matthews almost gets a TD in 200th straight start

Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews almost added a touchdown to the celebration of his 200th consecutive start, the longest active streak in the NFL.

The son of Pro Football Hall of Fame lineman Bruce Matthews lined up as an eligible receiver on second down from the Baltimore 5-yard line in the third quarter.

Matthews slipped into the end zone and was wide open, and Penix lofted a pass that forced Matthews to jump. He touched the ball with both hands, but the pass was too high and fell incomplete.

Ravens: Starting RG Andrew Vorhees (foot) was inactive after being listed as questionable. Emery Jones Jr. made his first career start. Rookie TE Matt Hibner left in the first half with a hand injury but returned in the third quarter. DLs Broderick Washington (ankle) and Travis Jones left in the fourth quarter.

Falcons: Penix predicted he will return next week from the rib injury. CB C.J. Henderson was listed as questionable with a groin injury in the third quarter. Matthews played after having been listed as questionable with a groin injury.

articles.title: Legendary MSU Men’s Track and Cross Country coach Jim Bibbs passes away at age 97
articles.summary: EAST LANSING, Mich. (WLNS-TV) – Jim Bibbs, the first black head coach in Michigan State athletics history who coached 52 individual Big Ten Champions and 26...
articles.body:
EAST LANSING, Mich. (WLNS-TV) - Jim Bibbs, the first black head coach in Michigan State athletics history who coached 52 individual Big Ten Champions and 26 All-Americans in a 19-year run leading the MSU men's track and cross country programs, passed away on Saturday at the age of 97.

MSU athletics officially announced Bibbs' passing in a press release Sunday. He was a pioneer of Spartan athletics and remains the longest-tenured head coach in MSU track and field history.

He was also an elite athlete himself. He earned All-American honors at Eastern Michigan in 1951 and tied a then-world record time of 6.1 seconds in the 60-yard dash. The record holder he tied at the time was none other than the legendary Jesse Owens.

A native of Ecorse, Mich., Bibbs coached Ecorse High School for four years before joining the MSU coaching staff in 1968. He led Ecorse to a state championship in his final season at the helm.

Bibbs is a member of six different halls of fame, including the Michigan Amateur Athlete Hall of Fame (Class of 1974), Eastern Michigan Athletics Hall of Fame (Class of 1979), Greater Lansing Area Sports Hall of Fame (Class of 2005), MSU Athletics Hall of Fame (Class of 2010), USTFCCCA Hall of Fame (2015), and the Detroit Public Schools Hall of Fame.

In the press release announcing his death, several MSU dignitaries offered their reflections on Bibbs' life and impact.

"Jim Bibbs is truly one of the icons of Spartan Athletics," wrote MSU men's basketball coach Tom Izzo. "He cared deeply about Michigan State University and even more passionately for the hundreds, if not thousands, of young men and women he impacted. His career is defined by its excellence, the barriers he broke, and the relationships he created.

"Coach Bibbs was one of the first people I met when I got to Michigan State, and as a young coach, I would walk up the stairs at Jenison many times each week for advice and perspective. The meaningful conversations we had still guide me today. He'll be remembered for his accomplishments with MSU Track & Field, but his impact and wisdom were felt throughout the entire department.

"Thirty-plus years after his retirement, he remained loyal to our University and an active supporter of MSU Athletics. My thoughts are with his family, friends and all the Spartans whose lives he enriched."

MSU Vice President and Director of Athletics Dan Bartholomae added "The thoughts and prayers of Michigan State Athletics are with the family and loved ones of Coach Jim Bibbs. I was fortunate to meet and speak with Coach Bibbs, and I was struck by the love and care he had for Michigan State, Spartan Athletics and the people within. The championships, the All-Americans, the records, they all speak for themselves. He was a game changer and his coaching and mentorship had a transformational impact on the lives of countless Spartans. He embodied the very best of what it means to be a Spartan."

articles.title: Who slept best last night: Max Verstappen
articles.summary: Two in a row for the four-time world champion. Bring on 2027...
articles.body:
It hasn't been a very interesting championship so far. Well… let's actually call it as it is: it's been pretty dull, with Kimi Antonelli grabbing the lead and refusing to let anyone touch it from early on.

That young Italian fella has certainly made sure we have nothing to get excited about in terms of the title fight. And even if the chances of him securing it in Austin in two weeks' time are relatively slim, you'd be forgiven for wishing it would happen sooner rather than later. Especially, if you're also sick of all this fake narrative about a possible comeback from George Russell or whoever else. No, let him just seal it right there and then, so we can enjoy the rest of the races, knowing there's nothing major left at stake.

Still, it's been quite an interesting season to observe. Not sure you follow, dear reader, but I'll try to explain…

Doesn't Max Verstappen 's latest win make you wonder whether everything you thought about the current season is actually true? Because it was quite clear, wasn't it, that Mercedes had just clawed its way back to where it belonged with that regulation change?

They've simply done it again, as in 2014: built the best power unit, produced the best chassis and are now cruising towards winning both championships this year - and not only that… They're surely now favourites for the next couple of years too, until they hit the ceiling of what is possible in terms of performance with this ruleset and their rivals finally manage to catch up.

How long did it take anyone to catch up back then? Until 2017 at least, when Sebastian Vettel could at least mount something resembling a challenge - and still lost out well before that year's championship ended. It really only happened in 2021, didn't it - when Red Bull finally produced the car and Verstappen was ready to take on the challenge against the team that had by then won god knows how many titles in a row.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing

Seeing how dominant Mercedes was until at least early summer this year, you wouldn't have been too wrong to assume we were heading into another era of Wolff and co domination.

I have to admit I did believe so. And I am sure many of you did, too.

That second win in a row for Verstappen at least provides some grounds for an alternative theory. Because the Mercedes run in early 2026 could be something different. Of course, you can't take anything away from them. They did indeed produce an incredibly strong engine, which is most likely - despite the ADUO rankings - the current benchmark. And the W17 is a very decent car, too - no doubt about that. But could it be that the early dominance of the Silver Arrows was simply a logical consequence of the events from last year and the beginning of this one?

After all, Mercedes wasn't involved in the title fight back in 2025, so could concentrate solely on getting ready for 2026 - unlike Red Bull and McLaren , who were forced, by each other, to keep pushing until the very end of last season.

The works team status certainly helped Mercedes gain an edge over McLaren in exploiting the new power unit better - and it's not even a theory, but an undeniable fact. Let's make it clear: it's not because Mercedes is hiding something from its customers - it's just natural that these customers don't have as much knowledge about it as Mercedes itself. And they needed time. That advantage, judging by McLaren's progress during the summer, is nearly gone now. Perhaps not entirely - but probably close to it.

It looked as if Red Bull had squeezed almost everything out of its development budget already in the first half of the year, but it appears that wasn't the case.

The Baku upgrade may have delivered the biggest hint so far that it's not going to be that easy for Mercedes to hold on to its advantage from early 2026 - and that its rivals aren't just catching up, but already have. After all, if you only count the last five rounds of the championship, Verstappen would be leading it, and with quite a healthy margin over Antonelli. Quite a comeback, isn't it? For a team that started the season almost in the midfield.

To underestimate Mercedes would surely be stupid. After all, there's no guarantee Wolff's engineers didn't throw all the files containing possible development plans for the W17 into the bin sometime in April, seeing how big the gap was to the opposition, and start working on next year's car. Could that be the reason the package introduced in Malaysia hasn't actually made the Silver Arrows quicker? But even if that's not the case, there's no reason to believe they'll continue struggling - if you can even call a team grabbing podiums on a bad weekend "struggling" at all.

But two wins in a row from a team that has also had its fair share of domination over the last couple of decades are no joke.

It would be interesting to hear what Max thinks about F1 2026 now, wouldn't it? Well, the context of the answer - even if you were to ask the question - is quite predictable. He'll say that the fact he's winning doesn't mean he thinks these regulations are now what Formula 1 needs - but he'd at least make a funny joke about it. And there's no doubt he feels a whole lot different now compared with the beginning of the year, when not only was he driving a car he didn't like - it was also painfully slow by his standards.

He chose to stick with the team even before it properly recovered to the position it is enjoying right now - and damn, what a wise move it was! You'd think the numbers in the contract in front of him would still be slightly lower nowadays, but, joking aside, these numbers won't mean much to him anyway, as he's already earned enough to finance the next few generations of Verstappens - but the fact that the team, which has lost so many people, still keeps delivering must be reassuring.

It's not going to change anything this year. Max can probably win a couple more races - but what must excite him the most right now is the prospect of 2027. If Red Bull keeps up the same pace, he's certainly going to have another go at the world championship.

It's also tempting to start imagining what a classic next year could be if Verstappen can challenge Antonelli for the big prize in equal machinery. Kimi is a generational talent, there's not a single doubt about it left. To some extent, he's just an improved version of Verstappen himself. Focused entirely on racing, bloody quick and consistent - and, at least until now, hasn't shown his dark side.

And that could be such a great thing for F1 itself, if there were a bit of sporting intrigue to distract attention from all the talk about power units. Just a good old-school battle between the greatest drivers in the world.

Max would surely enjoy it more than a repeat of 2023. Especially if not only Antonelli, but also Lewis Hamilton had a decent car to fight with - making it three generational talents battling for one big prize.

articles.title: Swansea's humble approach paying off - Cabango
articles.summary: Ben Cabango believes the Championship leaders' ethos is paying dividends as they go into games against Millwall and West Ham United.
articles.body:
Ben Cabango believes Swansea City's "humble" approach is paying dividends as they look forward to games against Millwall and West Ham United sitting top of the Championship.

The Wales defender helped his side once again hit back from 1-0 down, this time to beat Norwich , as the league campaign resumed following a four-game international break.

Cabango says boss Vitor Matos' ethos is paying off and building confidence at the Swansea.com Stadium.

"The main thing is we can feel real togetherness and the character," said the club's 26-year-old skipper.

"I feel like that's the third time I think we've come back from 1-0 nil down this season. I don't think there's ever any panic when we do go one-nil down."

Swansea have lost just once this season - away at Southampton - and have three wins and two draws at home.

"There's real belief right now in the squad, and we're playing with that confidence, aggression, like constantly, and that comes from the gaffer," added Cabango.

"Every game, he's always saying 'treat the next game like the cup final' and we don't look too far ahead.

"We're a humble squad and just pushing to get better every day."

Iconic Swansea manager John Toshack was there to see the comeback against Norwich, with Cabango acknowledging excitement among their fans at leading the promotion race cannot be ignored.

"I can already feel that, to be honest with you. The Swans fans [and] us as a team, we obviously are excited.

"But we've had a real good start. It's given us a great platform to build off, and we've just got to carry on."

Doing so will mean heading to Millwall on Tuesday - before hosting third-placed West Ham on Saturday - under no illusions as to what lies ahead.

"We know what to expect going to Millwall away," said Cabango.

"It's always going to be a physical, demanding game and the set pieces, the long balls. It's going to be a tough test and a different one to today [against Norwich].

"But we're going to obviously recover, prepare for it, and go in with that confidence and belief, like we do."

Cabango confident after intense Wales duty

On a personal level, it also means no let-up for Cabango after returning from top-tier Nations League duty that saw Wales lose to Portugal then Denmark twice, while also claiming Norway's scalp.

Cabango returned to club action feeling "confident" having earned wide praise for the way he marshalled Erling Haaland during Wales' win against Norway.

"Four games in two weeks is always going to be hard, and playing against the opposition you do, it's really intense," said Cabango.

He believes Swansea shook off their international-break "rustiness" against Norwich after an extended period away from domestic football.

"We came looking a new team really, and it was real positive to come from a goal behind and get the three points," he added.

articles.title: NFL Issues Explanation for Dre Greenlaw Ejection in Seahawks Game
articles.summary: The NFL explained why San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw was ejected against the Seattle Seahawks. The post NFL Issues Explanation for Dre Greenlaw...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks had some tense moments in their loss to the San Francisco 49ers, and a head official is explaining why they chose to toss a Niners linebacker from the game.

Officials ejected Dre Greenlaw after video replay showed him headbutting Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV. The Seahawks weren't able to take advantage, however, falling 32-29 to their NFC West rivals.

After the game, officials explained exactly why they singled out Greenlaw from a scuffle between multiple players.

As reporter Tom Pelissero of The Ringer noted, officials utilized a new rule to review the play and eject Greenlaw.

"49ers LB Dre Greenlaw was ejected for headbutting Seahawks LB Ernest Jones IV under a new rule that allows the league office to eject players for non-football acts even if they're not flagged," Pelissero wrote. "The NFL saw the replay and told officials to disqualify him."

Pool reporter Brady Henerson spoke after the game with Mark Butterworth, the league's vice president of instant replay. Butterworth explained that the league had a review process before ejecting Greenlaw, and that the call came from the league office after it was clear that he commited a non-football infraction.

"We have a specific process we go through," Butterworth said. "Troy Vincent let us know that the player was ejected, so then I communicated with the field to inform them that number 57 was ejected from the game for a non-football act."

articles.title: Míchel Sanchez Explains Selection Decision On Ajax Star Abdellah Ouazane
articles.summary: Michel Sanchez has spoken about Abdellah Ouazane's game time.
articles.body:
Abdellah Ouazane has made a very positive impression in his limited game time so far this season for Ajax . Ouazane has played most of his minutes so far on the left wing, but he can also play as a No. 10.

On the left wing, Oscar Gloukh has started in that position for the last three games. He is a player who constantly looks to make things happen, but his end product is often quite poor.

Julian Brandt has made the No. 10 position at Ajax his own and has been one of the standout players so far in the Eredivisie this season. He has scored four goals in eight Eredivisie games, and though he is yet to register an assist, he has created 28 chances, which is the most by any player in the Eredivisie, six more than Anis Hadj Moussa, who is second.

Most of Ouazane's minutes have therefore come as a substitute, and he has only started two Eredivisie games so far this season. Despite his limited minutes, he earned a call-up to the Moroccan national team in the recent international break and made his debut for the Atlas Lions.

Against NEC Nijmegen, Ouazane came on for the final 30 minutes, replacing Gloukh on the left wing. He once again looked good and showed glimpses of his quality.

In his post-match press conference after the game against NEC Nijmegen, Michel discussed Ouazane's playing time.

"He is an incredibly great talent," Michel said, speaking about Ouazane.

"As Ajax, we have the responsibility to give him plenty of minutes so that he can grow in his game. In my opinion, he still lacks a bit of consistency because Oscar and Brandt are currently playing in his position.

"So today it was my decision not to start him, but it is definitely our responsibility to give him plenty of minutes in the future. He is a great talent, and we have a lot of confidence in him as a player."

Ajax have several good options on the left wing. The club signed Simon Adingra to replace Mika Godts, but he only made his debut for the Amsterdammers against NEC Nijmegen, and prior to that game, he had not played in over two months due to injury. He played on the right wing on Saturday night, but is predominantly a left winger.

Gloukh has scored one goal and assisted four in the Eredivisie this season. He will play an important role for Ajax, but as mentioned already, his end product is inconsistent.

With Adingra still needing to gain match sharpness and Gloukh struggling for consistency, Ouazane should start on the left wing for Ajax in the coming games. He constantly makes things happen, and with regular game time, he will almost certainly score a lot of goals.

Ouazane has the talent to become one of the best players in the world, and Ajax need to make him a key player heading into the coming seasons.

articles.title: Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers shows respect to Mike Tomlin with postgame shirt after Colts win
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers paid tribute to former coach Mike Tomlin with a special shirt following Sunday’s 34-22 victory over the Indiana...
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers paid tribute to former coach Mike Tomlin with a special shirt following Sunday's 34-22 victory over the Indianapolis Colts . The veteran quarterback wore a shirt featuring one of Tomlin's familiar coaching reminders during his postgame appearance.

The shirt displayed the letters "DGBTTF," which stand for "Don't get beat to the flat." Rodgers, who previously spoke about his close relationship with Tomlin, explained that the message was a tribute rather than a warning directed at Indianapolis.

"No, it's not a warning," Rodgers said when asked about the shirt. "It's an ode to Mike T. He used to always say, 'Don't get beat to the flat.'"

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The phrase refers to a defensive responsibility in football, particularly preventing opponents from finding space for short passes near the sideline. The postgame shirt was highlighted by Blitzburgh on X , drawing attention to Tomlin's familiar coaching reminder.

Rodgers' gesture came after another productive performance for the Steelers offense. He completed 22 of 31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception.

The quarterback also completed his first 11 passes against Indianapolis, helping Pittsburgh establish an early offensive rhythm. His performance contributed to the team's third victory of the season.

Running back Jaylen Warren also played a major role in the win, producing 188 yards from scrimmage. He scored on an 80-yard reception and a 50-yard run as the Steelers pulled away from the Colts.

Pittsburgh improved to 3-2 with the victory at Acrisure Stadium, while Indianapolis dropped to 2-3. The result gave the Steelers another boost as they continued their regular-season campaign.

For Rodgers, however, the postgame shirt carried a message beyond the final score. His tribute showed that Tomlin's coaching words still hold meaning after the former Steelers coach stepped down following 19 seasons .

articles.title: Chargers’ Jim Harbaugh sends three-word message on key play leading to loss
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh had one big regret in their Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
articles.body:
The Chargers dropped their fifth consecutive game.

Los Angeles had a great chance to come away with its first win of the season, but they failed to capitalize on multiple plays, including a key 4th-and-1 that head coach Jim Harbaugh decided to go for with roughly 10 minutes left in the fourth quarter.

Harbaugh says that was his one big regret of the contest.

Up 17-10 on that fourth-down play, the Chargers had Justin Herbert try to rush for a first down. However, the Broncos ' defense stuffed the Chargers, and Denver took over at LA's 41-yard line.

Five plays later, Denver evened the game. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix connected with Courtland Sutton to tie it up, and Denver didn't look back.

From then on, it was tough sledding for the Chargers. Their offense fumbled the ball, and on their next series, Herbert threw an interception.

Los Angeles had a chance to win with 1:08 left, but with no timeouts, it was a tough hill to climb.

The game ended on a Herbert sack as time expired.

The Chargers dropped to 0-5 for the first time since 2003.

articles.title: “Don’t Think We Played Good”: Ravens Star Joins Jesse Minter to Call Out Locker Room Despite OT Win vs Falcons
articles.summary: The enigmatic play between the Baltimore Ravens and the Atlanta Falcons will stay up in Baltimore’s records for a long time. The Ravens took the game to over...
articles.body:
The enigmatic play between the Baltimore Ravens and the Atlanta Falcons will stay up in Baltimore's records for a long time. The Ravens took the game to overtime following a touchdown pass with just 40 seconds remaining on the clock. They then sealed the 30-23 win when Tyler Huntley scored on a one-yard touchdown run with less than 3 minutes remaining in overtime. However, there was one play that mattered the most that let the Ravens secure their big win.

Had it not been for Kyle Hamilton, the Falcons could have tied the game once again. But the safety intercepted Tua Tagovailoa's pass for Drake London and returned it for two yards. The clutch interception successfully limited the Falcons to 23 points. Yet, Hamilton believed that the Ravens' defense could have done better.

"I don't think we played good, for real," Hamilton said, as per The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec . "The third down stuff was crazy. We can do better."

Zrebiec also noted that Minter blamed himself for some of the third-down defensive issues, even though he delivered when it mattered the most. After all, his defensive calls stopped the Falcons from scoring a touchdown. In turn, that ended up bringing a win for the Ravens.

"I thought we played the run really well, which was a major focal point," Minter said in the postgame press conference. "We could've played it some third downs better, both schematically and just playing the plays. But [I'm] just really, really proud of our guys."

And as far as the offense is concerned, Minter had already emphasized that the offense doesn't need to change with Tyler Huntley as the quarterback.

Hamilton, during the postgame presser, noted that the Ravens lost the game against the Falcons "many times." He credited the offensive team for their eight-minute touchdown drives and two-point conversions. And when the defensive team stopped the opponent's offense, according to the safety, it was like them getting over a "dark cloud."

Nevertheless, Hamilton was content with the clutch interception that helped the Ravens have the last laugh. It's worth noting that Hamilton even got injured during the game and returned in the third quarter.

"Defense needed somebody to make a play," Hamilton told NBC about the interception that changed the direction of the game. "I was telling them in the locker room, we don't get paid for overtime, so we're out here for free, and I was trying to get home as quick as possible."

Right now, the Ravens are 4-1. They need to divert their attention to the Week 6 game against the Cleveland Browns . Of course, the way Deshaun Watson has been zooming past the defenses is certainly a call for action for the Ravens' defensive lineup.

articles.title: Alvarez vs M’billi boxing bout to go ahead despite Saudi airport attacks
articles.summary: Mexican boxer tells Turki Al-Sheikh he ‘fears nothing’ and will face M’billi in Riyadh on October 31 ‘no matter what’.
articles.body:
The world title fight featuring Saul “Canelo” ‌‌Alvarez and Christian M’billi will go ahead this month in Saudi Arabia despite attacks on the country’s airports, which have killed at least 14 people in Riyadh in two days, Saudi sports promoter Turki Al-Sheikh confirms.

Alvarez vs M’billi is scheduled for October 31 in the Saudi capital, which has repeatedly come under attack from Yemen’s Houthis, but Al-Sheikh sought to allay the doubts over the bout on Sunday.

One person was killed and 11 were injured on Sunday when a projectile struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, according to Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA).

A Houthi strike on the same airport on Saturday killed 13 people and injured more than 300, making it the deadliest attack on Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.

The Houthis claimed responsibility for all four strikes on Saudi airports before Sunday’s attack, which has yet to be claimed by any group.

Alvarez, who has held multiple world titles across several weight classes, will face WBC super-middleweight champion M’billi in a highly anticipated bout.

“Canelo reached out ⁠⁠and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens,” Al-Sheikh, chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority, wrote in a social media post. “He [Alvarez] fears nothing.”

The ‌‌Mexican boxer, a former two-time undisputed super-middleweight champion, has not fought since he was ‌‌beaten ‌‌by American Terence Crawford in September 2025.

articles.title: Steve Smith breaks Test fielding record as Australia dominate South Africa
articles.summary: Smith moves to 223 career catches, a record for fielders, as Australia bowl out South Africa for 284 in reply to 390.
articles.body:
Steve Smith has broken the Test record for the most career catches by a fielder as Australia have played themselves into a strong position on the third day of the first Test against hosts South Africa.

Smith held four catches on Sunday, taking his total to 223, as South Africa were bowled out for 284 in reply to Australia’s first innings of 390 at Kingsmead Stadium in Durban.

Nic Maddinson (17 not out) and Travis Head (10 not out) added 33 runs off just 5.4 overs to stretch Australia’s overall lead to 139 before bad light ended play for the third day in a row.

Maddinson, who laboured to a 33-ball duck in the first innings, hit two fours off Marco Jansen in the first over of the second innings and added a six off Wiaan Mulder before play was called off.

Australia’s bowlers applied relentless pressure on an easy-paced pitch and a succession of South African batsmen contributed to their own dismissals by playing poor shots.

Six Protea batters reached 30, but David Bedingham’s 49 was the top score.

Australian captain Pat Cummins took three for 54, and Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon claimed two wickets each as Australia’s long-serving bowling quartet combined with customary efficiency.

Smith started the day on 219 catches, one behind Joe Root of England.

He equalled the record when he caught Temba Bavuma. Smith, playing in his 126th Test, broke the record when he lunged to his left from second slip to hold a sharp edge from Bedingham off Cummins.

Smith was in the action again with a spectacular catch to dismiss Verreynne, again anticipating well at slip as the South African wicketkeeper made good contact with a reverse sweep that Smith held in an outstretched right hand.

His fourth catch was from an edge to slip by last man Anrich Nortje off the bowling of Beau Webster.

Smith’s career haul of 223 catches exceeds the total of all but 11 specialist wicketkeepers.

articles.title: What we learned from ‘guilty’ Man City’s win over Liverpool at Anfield
articles.summary: City beat Reds despite a hostile Anfield reception, but Premier League season still hangs in the balance.
articles.body:
Despite the hostile atmosphere created by Liverpool at Anfield for Sunday’s fiery clash, it was leaders Manchester City who had the last laugh with a superb 3-0 victory to maintain their perfect start to the Premier League season.

The noise centred on off-pitch matters as City returned to action after a bombshell ruling by an independent commission found them guilty of breaking more than 100 Premier League financial rules .

Enzo Maresca’s side could not have chosen a worse venue to restart their campaign after the guilty verdict.

Anfield for years has dished out an angry welcome to City.

On Sunday, the vitriol was at its highest with flags reading “cheats” and “114 charges”, a common sight in the merchandise on sale.

But even as the red smoke engulfed Merseyside and chants of “Cheating bastards” rang around the stadium, none of it could derail the defiant Manchester team, who turned the game around in six second-half minutes.

Ryan Gravenberch was sent off in the 62nd minute, reducing Liverpool to 10 men.

City capitalised on the one-player advantage as Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku scored in quick succession before Rayan Cherki added another, silencing the noisy Kop end of Anfield.

“It was not easy for the players after the last two or three weeks, but they dealt with the situation very well,” Maresca said after the match.

“I said during the week we need to learn how to deal with the outside noise but make our own noise, which is to win games. Our fans were singing at the end, so the noise was from us.”

Haaland, this season’s leading Premier League scorer with six goals, looked close to tears after the victory, which he described as a “lovely moment” and one that he said would stay with troubled City for a long time.

“It’s time to stay strong and stick together and do what you can do something about – stick together,” he added.

City win, but Premier League stuck in limbo

While City emerged unscathed from Sunday’s hostile face-off, the victory highlighted the uncertainty that now surrounds the remainder of the Premier League season.

Maresca’s side are at the top of the table with 18 points and a 100 percent record. Yet those results could count for nothing unless City, who deny any financial wrongdoing, are successful in their appeal against the guilty verdict.

No sanctions have been decided yet, but if City’s appeal fails, potential punishments include a significant point deduction and expulsion from the Premier League.

There is even the prospect of three Premier League titles being stripped from City, who won them from 2009 to 2018, the period to which the charges relate.

This guilty verdict on widespread financial impropriety thus leaves a question mark over every City result and what it means for other clubs.

“This is really bad for the Premier League, and it’s going to continue for a few months,” former Manchester United captain-turned-pundit Gary Neville told Sky Sports.

Earlier, Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola stressed that “ the uncertainty is not good for anyone ” while ex-Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said he hoped the appeal process does not drag on for months.

“There’s no way this can carry on to the end of the season because we’re all getting kidded,” Carragher said.

Then there is also the debate about City’s past successes. Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane argued that any title City won while engaging in financial wrongdoing would be difficult to celebrate.

“Some people might think it’s a bit stronger, but I wouldn’t feel I have earned a league title if I thought there was something dodgy going on in the background. Absolutely not,” he said.

“We talk about lads going out, giving their all and picking up injuries, … but that is your job. But you hope everyone is on the same page, being honest and doing things the proper way.”

What’s next for City and the Premier League?

Moments after City’s players broke into celebrations at the final whistle, Anfield’s DJ played the Fleetwood Mac song Little Lies over the loudspeakers.

Many would argue that was Liverpool’s, and by extension, their fans’ final act of defiance, but it certainly won’t be the last hostile reception City face at stadiums across England and beyond this season.

From now on, every time a team loses to City, their players and fans may be left feeling robbed.

Such is the state of the Premier League right now when its best-performing team is also its most controversial team.

Much of this stems from the uncertainty that City and 19 other clubs in the top flight are facing. What’s next? What sanctions, if any, await City? Will they be stripped of their titles?

“The Premier League have given their verdict, but we know that these things take time,” a Liverpool supporter told Al Jazeera outside Anfield on Sunday. “Hopefully, it doesn’t take years to discover what the end product is going to be.

“It’s heartbreaking. Having been a Liverpool fan for over 20 years, we’ve come close so many times, getting to 98 points, losing by one point. Those are the fine margins. … We could’ve been on 22 Premier League trophies.”

articles.title: Becky Lynch's Secret Injury, WWE Rumors on Roman Reigns' Schedule and AEW vs. NXT Ratings
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Seth Rollins divulged some previously unknown information Friday regarding an injury his wife, Becky Lynch, recently dealt with.

During an appearance on the Rich Eisen Show (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Rollins said Lynch had a "little fracture in one of her vertebrae" that rendered her unable to wrestle for about six weeks.

That likely explains Becky's four-month absence from in-ring action, as she last had a match in June before returning to the ring against Liv Morgan last week on Raw.

Lynch did have some physicality prior to last week's match, though, as she aided Stephanie Vaquer in her rivalry with Morgan.

Rollins noted that he was "a little concerned" about Lynch's back and how it would hold up, but he added that "it seems like all is well."

Becky was in action Saturday night at Money in the Bank, facing Vaquer and Morgan in a Triple Threat match for the Women's World Championship.

Lynch did not come away with the title, as Morgan pinned Vaquer to win, but The Man performed well and appears to be in good health following her absence.

Reported Reason for Reigns' Heavy Schedule

Roman Reigns has essentially worked a full-time schedule since winning the World Heavyweight Championship at WrestleMania 42, and that is reportedly by design.

According to Fightful Select (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), TKO requested that Reigns appear more regularly this year, and 2026 is expected to be The OTC's busiest year in quite some time.

Per Fightful, Reigns' schedule became a topic of conversation within WWE last week after the company announced his dates for October and November:

While Reigns' only advertised appearance for the remainder of October is the Oct. 19 episode of Raw, he is set for six appearances in November, including the Crown Jewel and Survivor Series premium live events.

In recent years, Reigns worked a part-time schedule and would be absent from WWE programming for extended periods of time.

Because of that, he has worked a limited number of televised matches, such as the seven bouts he had in 2025.

Reigns has already had that many matches thus far in 2026, and there are likely more to come, particularly in November.

After taking the world heavyweight title from CM Punk in the main event of WrestleMania 42, Reigns embarked on what has been a highly entertaining championship run with several excellent title defenses along the way.

Most recently, Reigns clashed with LA Knight at Money in the Bank on Saturday and weathered the proverbial storm to retain the World Heavyweight Championship.

Reported WWE, AEW Reaction to Head-to-Head Ratings

Both WWE and AEW were reportedly satisfied with their television ratings when they went head-to-head last Tuesday.

According to Fightful Select (h/t Mukherjee ), people within AEW were encouraged by the fact that the Grand Slam France edition of Dynamite had better ratings than last year's episode under similar circumstances.

Meanwhile, WWE reportedly celebrated a victory internally since NXT averaged more viewers than Dynamite.

Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter reported last week that NXT averaged 532,000 viewers with a 0.10 rating in the 18-49-year-old demographic, while Dynamite averaged 495,000 viewers with a 0.11 rating in the key demo.

Per Brandon Thurston of Wrestlenomics, last year's episode of Dynamite that went head-to-head with NXT averaged just 321,000 viewers with a 0.07 rating.

AEW loaded up last Tuesday's show with Will Ospreay defending the AEW World Championship against Kazuchika Okada, Mercedes Moné defending the AEW Women's World Championship against Queen Aminata and Darby Allin defending the TNT Championship against Kyle Fletcher.

WWE delivered a normal episode of NXT, headlined by Wren Sinclair winning a battle royal to determine the No. 1 contender for the NXT Women's Championship.

articles.title: Updated WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Match Card Predictions Including Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn
articles.summary: In the wake of WWE Money in the Bank, the futures of several Superstars and storylines are up in the air, as is the match card for Crown Jewel 2026.
articles.body:
In the wake of WWE Money in the Bank, the futures of several Superstars and storylines are up in the air, as is the match card for Crown Jewel 2026.

Last Saturday's show in New Orleans saw Tiffany Stratton and Penta emerge with the opportunistic briefcases, Oba Femi conquer Bronson Reed, Roman Reigns retain the World Heavyweight Championship and Liv Morgan regain the Women's World Championship.

As eventful of an evening as it was, there was also a general sense of dissatisfaction from fans regarding the lack of true change in the WWE landscape. Penta being elevated was an encouraging sign, but Reigns, Morgan and Stratton staying in the same spots hardly generated much excitement.

Reigns vs. Sami Zayn in a champion vs. champion clash seems to be set in stone for Saudi Arabia on Nov. 7, but the rest of the card won't be become clear until the upcoming episodes of Raw and SmackDown.

Until then, the following is the most likely lineup for WWE Crown Jewel 2026.

Men's Crown Jewel Championship: Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn

Since 2024, WWE has pit the Undisputed WWE champion up against the World Heavyweight champion in the main event of Crown Jewel, not only for brand supremacy but also the Men's Crown Jewel Championship.

The gaudy-looking title belt has no barring on WWE programming beyond Crown Jewel, simply bragging rights for whoever wins it. Cody Rhodes was the inaugural champ in 2024, followed by Seth Rollins in 2025.

This year's installment should see Roman Reigns rekindling his rivalry with Sami Zayn with both currently being in possession of the Undisputed WWE and World Heavyweight titles, respectively.

Of course, the two have history dating back to their days in The Bloodline together, specifically when Zayn severed ties with the group in early 2023 and unsuccessfully challenged Reigns for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship in his hometown of Montreal at Elimination Chamber.

They later reunited as part of a brief Bloodline reunion for WarGames at Survivor Series 2024, but Zayn is a drastically different character today than he was then, so the dynamic for a rematch between them at Crown Jewel will make it that much more interesting, despite the outcome not being in doubt.

Women's Crown Jewel Championship: Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green

The Women's Crown Jewel Championship has also been a staple of Crown Jewel for the past two years and is expected to once again be up for grabs at the 2026 installment.

Liv Morgan competed for the title and walked away with it by virtue of her victory over Nia Jax at Crown Jewel 2024. She has a chance to become the first two-time champ this year when she battles the reigning WWE Women's champion Chelsea Green.

That's assuming both women will still be holding their titles by then. Tiffany Stratton could realistically cash in her Money in the Bank briefcase on either of them, and it's no secret that her friendship with Green is strictly a transactional one for her.

Morgan just regained the Women's World Championship in a Triple Threat against Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch at Money in the Bank. She has no obvious challengers waiting in the wings, so this bout with Green will at least keep her busy for the next few weeks.

On paper, Morgan vs. Green isn't a barn burner by any means, and a win for Morgan feels like a foregone conclusion, but perhaps they'll surprise fans with strong in-ring chemistry and a quality contest.

Intercontinental Championship: Chad Gable vs. Ethan Page

Chad Gable hasn't had any significant storylines in his two months as Intercontinental champion, but he has maintained his momentum by taking on all comers and delivering some certified show-stealers.

His title defenses against Rey Mysterio and Dragon Lee in particular were phenomenal and showcased just how tremendous of a talent he is. He's also been at odds with Ethan Page, who has been denied an opportunity at the title by Gable until he can earn one.

His recent losses to Lee and Rey Fenix haven't helped his cause any, but Gable and Page are clearly on a collision course for a championship match, which would be a welcome addition to the Crown Jewel card.

Despite his setbacks, Page might pose the biggest threat to the Intercontinental title at the moment. In addition to being the perfect fit as champion, him putting Gable back in chase mode for a bit could heat up the championship picture.

The prestigious prize hasn't been on the line at a premium live event since SummerSlam, and WrestleMania 42 before that, so it deserves to be spotlighted on the Crown Jewel stage.

Last Man Standing Match: Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton

WWE did such an abysmal job handling the Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton rivalry heading into WrestleMania 42 that it was imperative they redeemed themselves at some point.

Sure enough, Orton resurfaced at SummerSlam to cost Cody the Undisputed WWE Championship, and the two have been at each other's throats ever since. Rhodes won their original encounter in fluky fashion at 'Mania and Orton avenged the loss in the rematch at Sunday Night's Main Event in early September, so the stage is set for a heated rubber match.

Since they were omitted from the Money in the Bank card, it only makes sense for them to have their big blowoff at Crown Jewel. Furthermore, the match must have some sort of a stipulation and Money in the Bank would be befitting of the feud.

Neither man can reenter the world title scene on SmackDown until they settle their score, and there's no reason to drag it out until Survivor Series. If the champion vs. champion matches at Crown Jewel aren't enough for the average fan, a marquee matchup between Rhodes and Orton would be a worthy attraction.

This should be where Rhodes gives Orton his comeuppance by punting him in the head and embracing that inner edge he's been eschewing for so long.

World Tag Team Championship: Oba Femi and Je'Von Evans vs. The Vision

It's possible WWE adds something to Crown Jewel that involves furthering the feud between The Bloodline and The 946, but they must first face off in six-man tag team action on Monday's Raw.

Instead, it would be a spectacle to see Oba Femi and Je'Von Evans join forces to fight The Vision for the World Tag Team Championship—and it would make total storyline sense, too.

Femi has been embroiled in a rivalry with The Vision since shortly following SummerSlam, first targeting Bron Breakker and then the returning Bronson Reed. As evidenced by his decisive win over Reed at Money in the Bank, Femi has demonstrated that he can hold his own against the group, but enlisting the help of an ally in Evans to take their tag titles would be the ultimate blow.

Evans has had his own issues with The Vision as of late. After being laid out by the faction on Friday's SmackDown, Evans was tossed off a ladder through the top of an ambulance by Breakker at Money in the Bank, so he could be looking for revenge as soon as Raw.

The red brand's tag team division has been depleted for months, so throwing Femi and Evans together as a makeshift tandem and giving them the tag titles would make for a fun run and kill more time for Femi until WWE is ready to put him in the hunt for the World Heavyweight Championship.

articles.body:
The 2026-27 NHL regular season started on Sept. 29, and at this stage, most teams are still evaluating their roster for any necessary changes. Meanwhile, injuries could have some clubs seeking depth from the trade market or from their AHL affliates.

Teams can also look to whatever talent remains in the unrestricted free-agent market. While the best players in what was a thin market were quickly signed in early July, a handful of veterans remain who could be useful for clubs seeking to address specific roster needs.

On Aug. 7, we ranked the top 10 available free agents . That list has shrunk significantly since then.

Some players, like forwards Eeli Tolvanen and Michael Bunting, defensemen Logan Stanley and Nick Blankenburg, and goaltender Cam Talbot, subsequently signed with new NHL teams. Others, like defenseman John Klingberg and goalie Connor Ingram, have retired.

Nevertheless, several notable veterans remain, including winger Patrik Laine and Vladimir Tarasenko. Follow along to see where they sit in our updated rankings of the noteworthy remaining UFAs.

Controversy followed Evander Kane for most of his 16 NHL seasons. His off-ice issues at times overshadowed his on-ice performance, and he seemed to wear out his welcome with the five teams he's played for during his NHL career.

Nevertheless, Kane has also proven his worth as a power forward, combining scoring ability with a physical, abrasive style. He's reached or exceeded 20 goals and 40 points nine times in his NHL career and has put up solid postseason stats with 32 goals and 55 points in 97 postseason contests.

Kane's reputation could scare off most teams. However, with a veteran-laden playoff contender, the 35-year-old left winger could be a worthwhile middle-six forward on a one-year deal.

In 16 NHL seasons, Adam Henrique earned a reputation as a reliable, versatile two-way forward who can play center or on the wing. He had 10 seasons with at least 40 points and went to the Stanley Cup Final with the New Jersey Devils in 2011-12 and with the Edmonton Oilers in 2023-24 and 2024-25.

Henrique earned that reputation because of his hockey smarts, playmaking abilities, and rising to the occasion in high-pressure situations. Those traits, combined with his leadership abilities, could make him an enticing veteran for clubs seeking a reliable checking-line forward.

Now 36, age and injuries could be catching up with Henrique. Nevertheless, he could be a cost-effective option on a one-year deal.

A creative, agitating winger, David Perron is a 19-season NHL veteran. He's been productive for most of his career, with 812 points in 1,239 regular-season games. Perron has also been a reliable playoff performer, with 64 points in 110 postseason games, winning the Stanley Cup with the St. Louis Blues in 2018-19.

Perron reached or exceed 40 points 13 times in his career, the latest a 47-point effort in 2023-24. He's capable of playing either wing and is a skilled playmaker who doesn't shy away from physical play.

Injuries hampered Perron over his last two seasons, leading to a decline in production for the 38-year-old winger. Still, he could be enticing for clubs looking for a physical scorer with leadership ability and playoff experience.

The youngest player on our ranking at 27, Philipp Kurashev is a six-year NHL veteran. A versatile forward who plays center or wing, he spent five seasons with the Chicago Blackhawks and last season with the San Jose Sharks.

Kurashev seemed to be a young forward on the rise in Chicago, culminating in a career-best 18 goals and 36 assists for 54 points in 75 games in 2023-24 alongside young phenom Connor Bedard. However, he struggled the following season, leading to his departure to San Jose as a free agent .

Injuries limited Kurashev to 20 points in 43 games last season with the Sharks, who opted not to re-sign him. Still, his age and playmaking potential he had in Chicago could make him an affordable, low-risk signing for teams looking for additional offensive skill.

A 17-season NHL veteran, James van Riemsdyk spent the past three seasons on affordable one-year contracts with the Boston Bruins, Columbus Blue Jackets, and Detroit Red Wings. The 37-year-old left winger had a respectable 15 goals and 31 points in 72 games with the Red Wings last season.

A big-bodied net-front left winger, the 6'3", 210-pound van Riemsdyk exceeded the 20-goal plateau seven times and 40 points eight times. He uses his size and long reach to generate scoring chances, while his large frame makes him effective in creating traffic in front of opposing nets.

Given his age and declining production, van Riemsdyk could be best used as a power-play specialist. His experience and offensive touch could make him effective for teams seeking some extra scoring punch.

A skillful two-way winger, Reilly Smith has had a productive 15-season NHL career. He had nine seasons with at least 40 points (including four with 50 or more points) and was a Stanley Cup champion with the Vegas Golden Knights in 2022-23. That earned him the No. 8 spot on our previous ranking.

Age seemed to catch up with the 35-year-old Smith over the last two seasons, bouncing from the Pittsburgh Penguins and New York Rangers before returning to the Golden Knights in 2024-25. His production tumbled last season to a career-low 26 points in 69 games

Still, Smith could have enough left in the tank for one more decent season. He could be a good addition to any club in the market for a skilled third-line winger.

Injuries and inconsistency plagued Patrik Laine in recent years, derailing his career as a high-scoring winger. Nevertheless, the 28-year-old Finn could be a good addition for teams that need a scoring boost, especially on the power play. His powerful shot earned him the No. 3 spot on our previous ranking.

When healthy, Laine is capable of putting up solid offensive numbers. The 6'5", 216-pound winger had 20 goals in 52 games with the Montreal Canadiens in 2024-25. From 2022 to 2024, he scored over 50 points at a point-per-game pace in two injury-shortened seasons with the Columbus Blue Jackets.

On Oct. 6, TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported that the Calgary Flames and Detroit Red Wings considered signing Laine. Because he was sidelined most of last season, LeBrun indicated he's eligible for an affordable, performance-bonus-laden contract, which could make him a fit for cap-strapped teams looking for scoring.

After a disappointing 2024-24 campaign with the Detroit Red Wings, Vladimir Tarasenko rebounded with 23 goals and 47 points with the Minnesota Wild. That bounce-back performance earned him the No. 1 spot on our previous UFA re-ranking.

On Oct. 8, TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported that Tarasenko received an offer from the Florida Panthers during the summer. He won his second Stanley Cup with the Panthers, but LeBrun doesn't think they will revisit their interest.

We previously noted that the 34-year-old Tarasenko proved he can be an effective middle-six winger with the right team. He's a two-time Stanley Cup champion whose experience would make him an invaluable addition to playoff contenders. At this stage, he could be an affordable one-year signing.

Stats via NHL.com , salary info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: 11 of the Most Wildly Expensive Athlete Cars
articles.summary: Star athletes tend to have many millions in disposable income. They often use that money to purchase flashy cars.
articles.body:
Star athletes tend to have many millions in disposable income. They often use that money to purchase flashy cars.

For some, these vehicles are incredibly expensive.

LeBron James, Erling Haaland and Cristiano Ronaldo are just three examples of world-famous athletes who have flexed their financial muscle on the road. They've all built up a spectacular collection of vehicles.

Here, we've assembled some of the most expensive athlete cars.

Due to the challenges of proving ownership, not all rumors are included. For example, big-name athletes such as Lionel Messi, Tom Brady and Aaron Judge are connected with million-dollar machines, but the reports are unconfirmed.

As a result, the list—carefully researched but potentially volatile—isn't comprehensive. Nevertheless, it sure is impressive.

It's only fitting that a world-famous wheelman has a spectacular car, right?

Fernando Alonso, a two-time Formula 1 champion and Aston Martin driver, recently purchased a "unicorn" Pagani Zonda Diamante Verde. He was spotted with the gorgeous V12 in Monaco.

While the price is unconfirmed, Carscoops noted that one-off Zonda 760 series models are trading for more than $10 million.

Among the athletes with these wildly expensive cars, there are many superstars from the soccer—yes, fútbol—world.

Karim Benzema, who rose to prominence as a striker for Real Madrid, is the first such example. A few years ago, he went through his garage and showed off a dazzling Bugatti Chiron in addition to several other pricey vehicles.

Most reports place the value of the Chiron hypercar north of $3 million.

During an interview with Sports Illustrated , Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić, a self-proclaimed car guy, joked that he has "too many" cars.

His featured ride is a Bugatti W16 Mistral Roadster, in which the Slovenian was seen arriving at a home game. Doncic owns one of the 99 units produced, all of which were pre-sold at a price north of $5 million.

Hopefully, we'll eventually be treated to the post-retirement car show he teased during his interview with SI .

Pro athletes we'd want to see play other sports

NFL Season Shaping Up To Be Unpredictable 🗣️

Along his ascent from RB Salzburg to Borussia Dortmund to Manchester City, Erling Haaland has accumulated a sparkling fleet.

Your favorite may be a Ferrari Monza SP2 or Ferrari 812 Superfast. You might prefer his Mercedes-AMG One or even appreciate his Rolls-Royce Cullinan. The list in Haaling's possession is as extraordinary as it is extensive.

But the spotlight is gleaming on the Bugatti Tourbillon, a $5 million hypercar that he reportedly bought with Norwegian billionaire Ole Ertvaag.

The second Formula 1 icon in the fold, Lewis Hamilton's priciest ride, is a proper match for his professional ties.

Hamilton, a driver for Ferrari, showed up to Monza in a coveted F40.

The story behind his purchase is spectacular as well.

In an Instagram post , Hamilton said the F40 sat in a garage for 30 years. "Master engineers and mechanics at the factory worked for weeks to bring her back to life," he said.

According to ESPN's Laurence Edmondson , the supercar has surpassed $8 million at auction at its highest value.

Among the best scorers of his generation, former striker Zlatan Ibrahimovic is known for an uncommon level of self-confidence.

"I am like a Ferrari among Fiats," he said in 2019 .

On its own, that quote is fantastic. It's even better knowing he purchased a Ferrari Monza SP2—worth approximately $2 million—around that time.

Also, for several years, Ibrahimovic has posted an image of an expensive car with the caption "Happy Birthday to Zlatan." In 2025 , that was a Ferrari F80 valued at $4.4 million. That'd be a heck of a birthday present.

The greatest player of his generation—at the very least—LeBron James has enjoyed a well-traveled career with four different NBA franchises.

When he's on the road, The King is moving in style, too.

LeBron's fascination with vehicles can be attributed to his childhood. "I was always inspired to have great cars and drive great cars," he told Vanity Fair . "That's just the little-inner-city-kid aspiration."

In a garage boasting Ferraris, a Lamborghini and more, James' reported prize is a Porsche 918 Spyder. The estimated value is north of $1.4 million.

In perhaps the most natural NBA transition possible, we shift from LeBron James to none other than Michael Jordan.

Back in 2024, Automobili Pininfarina shared a picture of the basketball legend taking delivery of a one-off Battista Targamerica. It's a specially built open-top variant that includes a cigar holder and humidor.

Due to the hypercar's customization—plus its ownership connection—its value is dynamic. It's likely above the typical $2-plus million for a Battista.

Jordan, who co-owns a NASCAR team, clearly has a love for the road.

Behind many years of stardom at European giants Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, Neymar is a world-famous playmaker on the pitch.

And the Brazilian's car collection isn't so bad, either.

Neymar added a $1.25 million Ferrari Purosangue SUV to his garage in 2025. That may be the jewel, although there are unconfirmed reports of a rare Lamborghini Veneno—one with an estimated value of $4.5 million.

Oh, and he has a replica Batmobile . Pretty sweet.

The options at Cristiano Ronaldo's disposal are nothing short of incredible.

Ronaldo, one of the greatest scorers in fútbol history, has used a portion of his immense wealth to amass a deep collection of vehicles. He showed off that impressive garage in an Instagram post .

Among the many high-dollar cars, the headliner is a white Bugatti Centodieci—an incredibly rare build that carries a $10 million price tag.

The total value of Ronaldo's fleet must be astounding.

Shortly before Max Verstappen ripped off four straight F1 titles, he had a chance to test the Aston Martin Valkyrie while in the prototype stage.

"It was a lot of fun out there," he said .

That's surely a vast understatement of the Valkyrie, which Verstappen now owns. He was seen driving the $3.5 million machine in a 2023 video .

Given his status as one of the most accomplished F1 drivers ever, Verstappen is quite literally the perfect person for such a stunning hypercar.

articles.title: Predicting When Penta and Tiffany Stratton Will Cash in WWE Money in the Bank Contracts
articles.summary: The WWE Universe watched in awe Saturday night as Penta and Tiffany Stratton scaled their respective ladders and retrieved briefcases that provide them guaranteed championship opportunities whenever they see fit.
articles.body:
The WWE Universe watched in awe Saturday night as Penta and Tiffany Stratton scaled their respective ladders and retrieved briefcases that provide them guaranteed championship opportunities whenever they see fit.

When might they choose to cash in and go for the championship gold?

Let's take a look with this preview of the next few months.

Tiffany Stratton cashed in her first Money in the Bank briefcase on the first SmackDown of 2025, and there are few better ways for her to reignite Tiffy Time than by running it back.

It adds a sense of excitement and intrigue to the new year, and it allows SmackDown to produce a high-profile angle right out of the gate.

Stratton has gotten close to WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green over the last two months, seemingly keeping her potential enemy close. That is a story that has legs, especially with Stratton possessing the briefcase, but there will come a time when WWE Creative has to pull the proverbial trigger or risk the fans growing tired of it.

Stratton kicking off the year with a cash-in, and heel turn, gets 2027 off to a hot start for the SmackDown women's division. It also puts Green in a position to make a run toward a rematch for the gold, whether that is before or at WrestleMania.

Assuming the plan remains for Oba Femi to challenge Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship at WrestleMania 43, and to have a long run after, the window for Penta to cash in his briefcase is smaller than it is with Stratton.

The luchador would seemingly have between now and the Royal Rumble to take his shot at dethroning Reigns and avenging his loss on September 14 in Mexico City.

An excellent setting would be Survivor Series, where Penta could take advantage of a grueling War Games match between The Bloodline and the 946 by rocking Reigns with a Mexican Destroyer, pinning the OTC, and capturing the top prize on the Raw brand.

He can then hold onto it for two or so months before dropping it back to Reigns and allowing the company to roll out the creative for the biggest match in recent WWE history.

The alternative is Penta cashing in on Oba Femi and having about as much success as anyone else has against The Ruler en route to his run as the company's new face.

articles.title: Raiders Week 6: Meet the Bills
articles.summary: This is Buffalo’s first game in Las Vegas since 2020
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are preparing to play their sixth regular-season game of the year and their third home game, against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. Kickoff is set for 1:25 p.m. PT.

The Bills are 3-1 going into Monday night's game at the Los Angeles Rams. So, the Bills are spending a lot of time on the West Coast this week.

For being AFC competitors, the Raiders and Bills haven't played a ton in recent memory. This will be just their fifth meeting since the 2016 season and their first since 2023 when the Bills beat the visiting Raiders 38-10 on September 17. This is just the Bills' second visit to play the Raiders in Las Vegas and it will be their first game there in front of fans. Expect a robust Bills' Mafia contingent.

articles.title: Alabama chides 'unacceptable behavior' of fans who threw objects at Georgia players
articles.summary: In a statement, Alabama said it is 'disappointed by the unacceptable behavior' of fans who were shown throwing objects at Georgia football players
articles.body:
Alabama said it is "disappointed by the unacceptable behavior" of some of its fans who were seen throwing objects at Georgia players after the Bulldogs' 20-17 victory against the Crimson Tide on Saturday, Oct. 10 at Bryant Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Alabama .

In a statement provided to USA TODAY Sports, the university added that it is "in the process of gathering information."

"Alabama takes matters of fan conduct seriously and expects everyone at our events to demonstrate respect to the student-athletes, coaches, staff, officials and visitors," the school said in the statement. "Such conduct will not be tolerated."

The misbehavior came not only following a close home loss to what's become a bitter rival, but after a series of controversial calls .

In the third quarter, what was initially ruled an interception by Alabama linebacker QB Reese at the Georgia 25-yard line was determined to be an incomplete pass after a video review, a decision that was criticized by ESPN analyst Kirk Herbstreit. The Bulldogs didn't score on the drive, but because of the reversal, the Crimson Tide were denied a potential scoring opportunity in a game they lost by only three.

In the fourth quarter, safety KJ Bolden appeared to lower his head and hit receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams in the helmet, dislodging the ball in the process. Coleman-Williams was forced to leave the game to undergo an evaluation, though officials did not penalize Bolden for targeting.

Later, on what would be Alabama's final drive of the night, Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell tried to connect with Rico Scott for what would have been a go-ahead touchdown. Replay showed Bolden and Braylon Conley made contact with Scott before he had a chance to bring the ball in.

Russell was sacked for a 9-yard loss on the next play, a third-and-10 that took Alabama out of range for a potential game-tying field goal.
