articles.title: Texas softball adds to 2028 recruiting class with commitment from infielder Ainsley Morvan
articles.summary: The pledge of infielder Ainsley Morvan gives Texas softball four commitments for the 2028 recruiting class
articles.body:
Texas softball picked up its fourth member for the 2028 recruiting class with a weekend pledge from infielder Ainsley Morvan.

A Louisiana native from the Texas border town of Logansport, Morvan has lots of Longhorns ties when it comes to recruiting. She plays for the Texas Bombers Gold travel ball club alongside fellow 2028 Texas commitments infielder Michaela Landers and Zoey Abdullah as well as 2027 pledge Emree Masaad. Her travel squad also has former Texas pitcher and USA Softball Hall of Fame member Cat Osterman as an assistant coach.

Morvan, a 5-foot-3 left-handed hitter, isn't a slap hitter despite her size. She hammered 22 home runs last season for Logansport High School, which went 22-11 and reached the third round of the Louisiana state playoffs.

Morvan ranks as the 77th player in the Rivals 2028 class rankings. She joins a class headlined by Rivals No. 1 recruit infielder Michaela Landers and Line Drive Media No. 4 recruit pitcher Lauren Schellhammer The class also includes Abdullah, the 61st-best player in her class, according to Rivals.

The Longhorns rank 10th in the 2028 Rivals team rankings prior to Morvan's commitment.

The Longhorns have won back-to-back national championships and will enter the 2027 season as one of the favorites behind returning stars such as pitcher Teagan Kavan , first baseman Katie Stewart and center fielder Kayden Henry. They continue fall ball at 6 p.m. Tuesday at McCombs Field against Texas State.

articles.title: QPR trio nearing returns – but defender suffers another setback
articles.summary: Ilias Chair, Koki Saito and Rumarn Burrell are all closing in on returns for QPR, providing Julien Stephan with some welcome positive injury news.Chair is ne...
articles.body:
Ilias Chair, Koki Saito and Rumarn Burrell are all closing in on returns for QPR, providing Julien Stephan with some welcome positive injury news.

Chair is nearing the end of his rehabilitation after missing the last four games, while Burrell and Saito have both resumed partial training.

"He worked very well individually. He's close to coming back collectively with us," Stephan said on Chair.

"Depending on the last scan he will have at the end of the week and how he restarts collectively with us, we are at the end of the rehab with him.

"He worked very well. He's very positive. Everyone is very positive around him about the rehab, so I think he's in a good place now to come back quite quickly."

Burrell is also progressing after returning to partial training.

"He restarted some individual sessions, so progressing well," Stephan said.

"So, we have to see now how the situation evolves before thinking about collective sessions."

Saito is also expected to miss Wednesday night's Championship clash with Derby County but Stephan is hopeful he will be back soon.

However, Tariq Lamptey is set to miss Wednesday's clash after picking up an ankle injury against West Ham on Friday .

articles.title: Ravens vs. Falcons: Good, bad and ugly from Baltimore’s overtime win
articles.summary: The Ravens survived a hard-fought battle against the Falcons, turning up the heat late for an exciting win.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens had to earn every bit of their victory over the Atlanta Falcons , and it certainly wasn't pretty for much of the evening. The offense stumbled early. The defense missed opportunities to create turnovers. Even the always sure-handed Zay Flowers dropped a pass that would have moved the sticks on third down.

Baltimore spent much of the first half playing catch-up, making mistakes and leaving points on the field. Tyler Huntley eventually settled in, Derrick Henry and Justice Hill provided a much-needed spark , and Tyler Loop continued his remarkable climb as one of Baltimore's most dependable weapons.

When the game reached its defining moments, the Ravens found another gear. That forced overtime before delivering the decisive blow. Baltimore's resilience was impressive, but the performance also raised concerns that won't disappear just because the Ravens walked away with another win. Here's the good, the bad, and the ugly from Baltimore's hard-fought win over the Atlanta Falcons .

The good things we saw during the Ravens' win over the Falcons

The rushing attack found its footing. Atlanta entered the game allowing just 48.1 rushing yards per contest. That was the best mark in the NFL through four weeks. Baltimore had already piled up 90 rushing yards by the end of the first quarter, with Derrick Henry accounting for 49. He finished with 102. Baltimore as a whole ran for 208. That physicality gave the Ravens a foundation when the passing game struggled.

Tyler Huntley delivered a quarterback sneak worth celebrating. A 15-yard quarterback sneak behind Vega Ioane reminded everyone that Baltimore's quarterback can contribute to the ground game in unexpected ways. The play lacked subtlety, but it had plenty to love in its execution.

Tyler Loop keeps raising the bar. After Baltimore brought in another kicker to challenge him, Loop has earned Ravens fans' trust, and they now serenade him after successful kicks. For the second consecutive week, he connected on a long-distance field goal as time expired in the first half, keeping Baltimore within reach during a largely forgettable opening stretch. Now, be honest. When was the last time anyone expected to utter the words 'Loop is keeping the Ravens in the game?'

Trenton Simpson continues to make an impact. Another sack gave Simpson a team-leading three on the season. Baltimore needs more consistent pressure from its defense, and Simpson is providing encouraging production there.

Justice Hill supplied the lightning to Henry's thunder. Hill's 47-yard dash set up Baltimore's first touchdown: an 18-yard catch-and-run by Henry, punctuated by a stiff-arm. After waiting for the two backs to complement each other, it was encouraging to see Hill break free for explosive gains. Mark Andrews couldn't haul in the two-point conversion attempt, however, capping a difficult evening for the tight end.

Baltimore refused to fold late. Facing the need for a touchdown, a two-point conversion, and a defensive stop to force overtime, the Ravens produced one of their best drives of the night. The six-play, 71-yard march tied the game at 23 and gave Baltimore another chance.

The Ravens finished the job in overtime. Baltimore won the coin toss and put together a clock-consuming drive that lasted 7:03 of the 10-minute extra period. Huntley's one-yard quarterback sneak capped the possession, and Kyle Hamilton delivered the final blow by intercepting Tua Tagovailoa, who entered after Michael Penix Jr. was injured.

The bad news from the Ravens' win over Atlanta

Miss ing out on opportunities. Two Ravens defenders got their hands on the ball during Atlanta's opening offensive series, but neither turned it into an interception. Those missed chances might seem minor in isolation, but turnovers can swing close road games, especially against an offense that can score quickly.

Mark Andrews had a night to forget. Andrews dropped a potential touchdown on Baltimore's opening offensive drive. Then lost a fumble on the next possession that Jessie Bates returned for a scoop-and-score. The Ravens cannot afford to give opponents free points, particularly when their offense is struggling to establish a rhythm.

Ravens tight end Matt Hibner was carted to the locker room with a hand injury . Baltimore already lost Durham Smythe to a season-ending Achilles injury last week, leaving the tight end room even thinner. Broderick Washington and Travis Jones left with injuries during the fourth quarter. If there's a silver lining in all of that, Josh Cuevas has shown flashes of real potential, but the injuries are hard to ignore.

The Ravens are now 4-1 and lead the AFC North, but this win doesn't erase the problems that surfaced along the way. Baltimore showed resilience when the game was on the line, yet the penalties, missed turnovers, offensive inconsistency, and mounting injuries remain concerns heading into the next challenge.

The Cleveland Browns visit Baltimore at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, Oct. 18. The Ravens will win, but they'll need a cleaner performance to keep their place atop the division.

articles.title: Vikings snap counts and notable PFF grades from dominant win over Saints
articles.summary: What can we learn from this week's playing time numbers and Pro Football Focus grades?
articles.body:
The Vikings put together their most impressive all-around performance of the season on Sunday as they improved to 5-0 with a road win over the Saints. With the way they dominated yardage and time of possession, this would've been a Minnesota romp if not for two poorly-timed red zone fumbles that led to both Saints touchdowns. Even with the fumbles, it was a ten-point win that hardly felt in question for most of the fourth quarter.

Let's dive into this week's snap counts and PFF grades before the Vikings head into their bye week.

Vikings offensive snaps vs. Saints (out of 71)

Hockenson left the game after just two snaps to be evaluated for a concussion and did not return. The Vikings were already without Josh Oliver. That left them to lean on Bartholomew (who ended up with five receptions) and Yurosek, who was making his season debut.

Aaron Jones once again dominated running back snaps, but it sounds like Jordan Mason will be back after the bye week to return the position to a committee approach. With no Jordan Addison, Jennings finished second in wide receiver snaps but did not have a catch on one target. Murray had him open for a touchdown on one occasion and didn't pull the trigger.

Jeshaun Jones played only six snaps but made his impact felt with a 32-yard reception. Dallas and Claiborne were also among the ten Vikings players with at least one catch.

Top 5 PFF grades on offense (min. 20 snaps)

Murray earned a very strong grade for the second consecutive week. Getting Jefferson back was a big boost to the offense. Bartholomew acquitted himself well in easily the most snaps of his career, as did Yurosek (65.5 grade). Jones getting a grade that good despite having a fumble tells you how effective he was.

The Vikings' lowest grade went to Price for his 14 snaps and key fumble. Jennings, Van Demark, Felton, and Huber also earned lower grades.

Vikings defensive snaps vs. Saints (out of 45)

For the second straight week, the Vikings' offense was on the field for far more snaps than the defense was. The top eight players in snaps are the same as always. Ingram-Dawkins and Jackson also saw quite a bit of playing time, following by Smith and Rodriguez and Pierre. There were only scraps left for Van Noy, Pace, and the rookies.

Top 5 PFF grades on defense (min. 20 snaps)

The usual suspects make up the top grades as well. Jackson and Van Ginkel weren't far behind. Murphy had two interceptions, Cashman led the team in tackles, Rodgers was sharp in coverage, Redmond was a menace against the run, and Turner had four pressures, even if he finished with no sacks for the first time this season.

Lower grades went to Metellus, Rodriguez, Wilson (despite a team-high five pressures), Smith, and Ingram-Dawkins.

articles.title: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly vs. Kentucky
articles.summary: Sloppy play, coaching, and officiating throughout LSUs loss to Kentucky
articles.body:
LSU has extended its losing streak on the road. In a game where the Tigers had opportunities to win, they allowed Kentucky to hang around, and the Wildcats were able to finish the game with a victory. We will get right into it.

Not much good came out of this game, but Sam Leavitt has now had three consecutive games completing over 70% of his passes, a stretch he has never accomplished before. While he was still a little limited in his ability to run, it was good to see that his hamstring is healing.

The passing game as a whole is beginning to come along. This was a game in which LSU was held to only 2.6 yards per carry in the running game but was still able to move the ball between the 20s and gain over 400 yards of total offense.

The defense. This segment could end with just those two words.

The defense gave up 35 points to Kentucky, and while this is a really good Kentucky team, the defense has been the one side of the ball that has been great. It was the side of the ball that Lane Kiffin even said this team would have to lean on.

Well, twice now on the road this season, the Tigers' defense has not shown up.

This week, it just felt like they were not prepared. The off-ball coverage that has not been working well this year was something that was being utilized again. More shocking, though, was the lack of a pass rush and the inability to stop the run. Those were the two staples of this defense.

Kentucky ran the ball for 155 yards on 32 carries, averaging 4.8 yards per rush. Kenny Minchey threw for 246 yards, and LSU did not force a single turnover.

In football, if you truly have a good defense, it travels with the team. This defense has not shown the ability to consistently live up to the standards it has set at home when playing on the road this season.

This was by far the worst coaching performance on both sides of the ball. The offensive scheme designed to run the ball did not work at all. I'm not sure what they saw on film, but it did not work.

This offense needs to be able to play a complete game against tougher competition.

Getting a delay-of-game penalty after a timeout, not having the correct personnel on the field at times, and not being sure of what to do in pivotal situations were all showcased on Saturday night.

Hopefully, a game like this will wake them up.

Going back to the defense, you can't allow teams to keep getting early leads on the road. In the second half, the defense held Kentucky to six points, but they gave up those points in bad situations.

There were also some coaching decisions that took place that were beyond bad. That discussion will come later.

Two more turnovers for Sam Leavitt. So far, Leavitt is the only quarterback in the country with an interception in every single game this season. This is also the most interceptions he has thrown in a single season, and this was only game number six.

The turnovers have to stop. They actually hurt the team in a really bad way in this game.

The officiating throughout the SEC has been atrocious, and it was on full display Saturday night in Lexington.

Do not confuse the frustration being conveyed with the reason LSU lost. LSU lost because it did not execute the way it needed to. The referees just made it feel worse.

There were several key moments when flags should have been thrown and were not.

Multiple players were blocked in the back on that punt return touchdown. Sam Leavitt was hit clearly after a whistle was blown on a dead play, and not just hit, but slammed to the ground, with no flag thrown.

There was a controversial targeting call that was not upheld, when LSU fans know all too well the letter of the law regarding targeting after suffering at the hands of that penalty with Devin White and Whit Weeks.

And the most critical penalty that was not called was an obvious false start that took place on the two-point conversion attempt.

On the play before Kentucky actually won the game, the Wildcats came out in a different formation. They had their tight end, Willie Rodriguez, line up as the quarterback under center. The tight end lined up to the left flinched as Rodriguez was calling for the snap.

The referees blew the play dead, and a flag was apparently thrown, or was about to be thrown, before the officials waved it off, to everyone's surprise, because they claimed Kentucky head coach Will Stein had called a timeout.

This game was horribly officiated, but it's been ugly all over the league. See what happened at the end of the Alabama vs. Georgia game to fully understand how bad it has been.

The hesitation from Lane Kiffin to be Lane Kiffin.

Kiffin was brought to LSU for his brash, aggressive, against-the-grain offensive mindset. Well, throughout this season, that has not really been on display, and this Saturday night, Kiffin had the opportunity to be the most Lane Kiffin he could possibly be at LSU.

Fourth-and-1 at the 43-yard line, under two minutes remaining, and Kentucky had no timeouts left.

Lane Kiffin sent the offense out on the field and attempted to get the defense to jump offsides instead of running a play.

That's not the Lane Kiffin LSU sought after and brought to Baton Rouge.

That Lane Kiffin, on Saturday, decided to be nice and give Kentucky a chance instead of being that dangerous threat who keeps opposing coaches on their toes because they never know when he will attempt to go for the win.

This felt like a version of Kiffin who was coaching not to lose the game.

And that's not what LSU needs from Lane Kiffin. That is an ugly version of himself because that's not who he has showcased himself to be as a coach.

This will be something that sticks with him for the rest of the season.

Hopefully, Kiffin will be able to find a balance with his aggressiveness rather than abandon it altogether.

What were some things that stood out to you? Share your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: 49ers Star Drew Greenlaw Ejected After Headbutting Seahawks Rival in Heated Scene
articles.summary: The incident occurred in the first half of the NFC West clash on Sunday, Oct. 11
articles.body:
Dre Greenlaw was ejected after a late-hit penalty led to a sideline confrontation with Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones IV

Coach Kyle Shanahan said Greenlaw needs to be smarter after the third ejection of his career

The 49ers remained undefeated at 5-0 after their 32-29 win over the Seahawks

Tensions escalated well before the final whistle of Sunday's NFC West clash.

San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw was ejected in the first half of the team's eventual 32-29 road win over the rival Seattle Seahawks for headbutting a helmetless opponent in a fiery scene on Sunday, Oct. 11.

The drama unfolded in the second quarter when Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold rushed for five yards and stepped out of bounds on his own sideline, as Greenlaw, 29, came in and was flagged for a late hit. Several Seahawks players then entered the scene, with Greenlaw and Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones IV having words, according to ESPN , before the Niners star connected with a helmet-less Jones , 26.

Officials then confirmed Greenlaw's ejection, the third of his career.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

"He knows he's got to be smarter," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said after the Week 5 win.

Greenlaw, who got the boot in 2022 over a late hit against Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert and again the following year after an altercation with Philadelphia Eagles security chief Dom DiSandro, is likely facing further discipline from the league. He was fined nearly $12,000 on Saturday, Oct. 10 for unsportsmanlike conduct, stemming from an incident last week when he yelled at the Denver Broncos sideline, per ESPN.

"That's how it is," Shanahan said postgame. "You're going to get baited big time, especially when you're on their bench. They're going to get close, and they told me that he head-butted a guy without a helmet. So, if that's exactly what happened, then we got to be a lot smarter than that. Can't do that."

Greenlaw, an eight-year veteran on his second run with the 49ers after spending the 2025 season in Denver, was suspended for one game last season when he ran toward official Brad Allen and was accused of "verbally" threatening him, according to ESPN.

San Francisco now sits atop the NFC West at 5-0 following Sunday's game, while the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks are in second at 3-2.

articles.title: Michigan will stick with Bryce Underwood as the starting quarterback
articles.summary: Coach Kyle Whittingham says Jason Beck remains the offensive coordinator, but the turnover problem must be corrected or "something's got to give."
articles.body:
ANN ARBOR – Bryce Underwood remains Michigan's quarterback and Jason Beck the team's offensive coordinator as the limping Wolverines , coming off a bye after back-to-back Big Ten losses, prepare for Penn State.

Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham, in his first year with the program, after the loss to Minnesota on Oct. 3 called this season – the Wolverines are 3-2, 0-2 Big Ten – "maybe the biggest challenge I've had" in 40-plus years of coaching. But he also said while he would evaluate the players and coaches, this wasn't a time to panic.

That said, the only major change he's seeking as the Wolverines press forward with seven remaining regular-season games is in terms of fixing the turnover margin and protecting the ball. The Rhino package, utilizing an extra lineman and a big part of Beck's offense, will continue, Whittingham said.

"Jason will call plays and Bryce is our guy and we move forward," Whittingham said Monday, Oct.12 at his weekly news conference. "All positive but continuing to stress to everybody about the importance of taking care of the ball. And with (Underwood) touching the ball every single snap, he's a big part of that. If we don't get this turnover thing fixed rapidly, then something's got to give."

Underwood had two interceptions on back-to-back throws against Minnesota, and the Wolverines also had a fumble on punt return, which will see a change from Andrew Marsh this weekend against Penn State. Michigan is minus-4 in turnover margin, among the nation's worst, and had four interceptions and five fumbles.

Backup quarterback Tommy Carr took half the snaps with the first team last week, but Whittingham said that was by design as the second-teamers got more work during a bye week. Whittingham did not rule out giving Carr a series or inserting him in games as a changeup to Underwood.

"To be determined," Whittingham said. "He sure looks good in practice like he has throughout spring and fall camp. And his small, tiny sample size that he had in the (UTEP) game was positive. But right now, like I said, Bryce is our guy, and if we think that giving Tommy a series or two helps our chance to win, then you will see that."

Who you won't see returning punts is Marsh, who has twice muffed punt returns this season.

"We'll have a different returner back there, and that's due to a couple of reasons, not just putting the ball on the ground, but some injury reasons," Whittingham said. "And so we will have a different returner - I won't say who that is yet - returning punts this week."

▶Kickoff: 3:30 p.m. Saturday, Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor

▶Records: Michigan is 3-2, 0-2 Big Ten; Penn State is 3-3, 0-3.

▶Series: Michigan leads 17-10 (Last meeting: Michigan defeated Penn State 24-15 on Nov. 11, 2023).
authors: Angelique S. Chengelis, The Detroit News

articles.title: Fans hand out grades to Bengals for win over Dolphins
articles.summary: The results are in and fans say the Bengals passed the test against the Dolphins.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals beat the Miami Dolphins 31-24 at Hard Rock Stadium in Week 5 to move to 3-2 on the year and are starting their bye week.

The offense was more balanced , the defense got three turnovers and special teams almost opened the game with kickoff return for a touchdown. While the margin of victory was only one score, the game was never really in doubt in the second half.

Cincinnati will head to Baltimore to face the Ravens in Week 7 after the bye. The Ravens (4-1) are coming off a win over the Atlanta Falcons and head to Cleveland to face the Browns on Oct. 18.

Bengals grades from fans/readers of Cincinnati.com for win over Dolphins

Bengals grades from Cincinnati.com staff

Here's how our gameday staff graded the Bengals in the win:

Joe Burrow's four touchdown passes stood out the most on the final stat sheet, but the near 50-50 balance of runs and passes were the story of the day . The efficient run game – 3.8 yards per carry – allowed the pass game to operate smoothly and led to the spectacular 45-yard touchdown catch by Ja'Marr Chase near the end of the third quarter.

Defensive back Jordan Battle backed up his comments earlier in the week with a two-interception performance against Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis. The defense won the turnover battle 3-1 and kept Miami from making the game close until there was less than a minute remaining. Miami gashed the Bengals defense for 217 rushing yards, but the turnovers and pivotal sacks on Willis made the day for Cincinnati.

Kicker Evan McPherson now owns the franchise record for consecutive field goals made (22) and will have a chance to add to that in Week 7 against the Ravens. Wide receiver Dohnte Meyers also took the opening kickoff 81 yards to give the Bengals great field position to start the game and set the tone. The only real issue on special teams was when Meyers went out of bounds after fielding a kickoff to pin the Bengals at their own 4-yard line, which is why this isn't an A.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 6 Stock Watch Risers: Is Jaylen Warren an RB1 Lock? Can Managers Trust Mike Evans?
articles.summary: Break down the biggest Week 5 fantasy football risers, including Jaylen Warren, Aaron Rodgers, and Mike Evans. Plus, buy/sell verdicts on whether their produ...
articles.body:
Fantasy Football Week 5 Stock Watch Risers: Is Jaylen Warren a RB1 Lock? Can You Trust Mike Evans?

Target share shifts, injury-forced backfield takeovers, and monster passing outputs defined Sunday's Week 5 slate. While seeing massive stat lines creates instant waiver wire and trade-target buzz, smart fantasy football managers know how to separate sustainable, season-long momentum from temporary, circumstantial spikes.

Let's take a look at five key players who surged this week, along with the fantasy verdict on whether they represent the Real Deal or Fool's Gold.

Fantasy Football Stock Watch: Week 5 Risers

Jaylen Warren delivered an absolute masterclass in Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory over the Colts. Operating as the true engine of the Steelers' offense with Rico Dowdle sidelined, Warren racked up 101 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, while adding 6 receptions for 87 yards and another score through the air-highlighted by a spectacular 80-yard house call on a dump-off pass.

Warren has put together three straight elite performances, showcasing explosive upside both as a runner and a pass-catcher. Even when Dowdle returns to split touches, Warren has clearly seized the high-value touches in this offense and proved he has game-breaking ability every time he touches the ball. He is firmly locked into the weekly RB1 conversation.

Aaron Rodgers stayed red-hot in Week 5, completing 22-of-31 passes for 235 yards and 3 touchdowns in a win against Indianapolis. This marks his third consecutive game throwing for three touchdowns, as the veteran signal-caller continues to look comfortable in Mike McCarthy's scheme.

While Rodgers' high efficiency and 10:4 TD:INT ratio are impressive, fantasy managers need to exercise caution. Much of his output has been fueled by massive run-after-catch plays from his playmakers (such as Warren's 80-yard touchdown) rather than heavy passing volume. He's also dealing with wide receiver injuries with Michael Pittman on IR and Roman Wilson now hurt. Without offering any rushing baseline, Rodgers remains dependent on multi-touchdown games to deliver QB1 fantasy finishes. He is a fine superflex option or streamer, but don't expect set-it-and-forget-it top-8 QB numbers rest-of-season.

Isaiah Likely was the ultimate stat-sheet stuffer in Week 5, erupting for 11 catches on 13 targets for 94 yards and 2 touchdowns. This follows a Week 4 performance where he also commanded double-digit targets, cementing his role as a featured target in the Giants' passing attack.

Tight end is often a fantasy wasteland, but Likely's recent usage isn't a fluke. The Giants have consistently schemed to get him involved, and he is being drawn up as a primary read in key areas of the field-especially in the red zone. With consecutive weeks of elite target volume, Likely has officially transcended streamer status and vaulted himself into the top tier of weekly tight end starters.

RB Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots

Rhamondre Stevenson turned in another solid fantasy day during New England's 45-17 blowout win over the Raiders, rushing 13 times for 64 yards and a touchdown while adding 3 catches for 21 yards. It marks back-to-back games with double-digit fantasy points and a goal-line score for the veteran back.

The biggest takeaway for Stevenson's outlook moving forward is the health of TreVeyon Henderson, who exited Week 5 early due to an ankle injury. If Henderson misses extended time, Stevenson steps right into a bell-cow volume role behind a Patriots offense that is clicking on all cylinders. Even in a split backfield, Stevenson gets the high-leverage goal-line carries, making him a reliable RB2 with or without Henderson.

Mike Evans enjoyed his best performance of the season in a 32-29 win over Seattle, hauling in 7 of his 10 targets for 113 yards and a touchdown. It was his first double-digit target game of the campaign and his first 100-yard receiving output.

While Evans remains a Hall of Fame-caliber receiver, his sudden explosion was heavily dictated by circumstance. San Francisco's wide receiver corps has been completely decimated by injuries , leaving Evans as virtually the only healthy wideout of note on the roster. Opposing defenses will quickly adjust by rolling safety coverage his way, and his overall efficiency could struggle when key pass-catchers return to re-establish the offensive balance. Enjoy the big week, but treat Evans as a touchdown-dependent WR2 option rather than an elite WR1.

articles.body:
On the morning of their Media Day on September 25, the Dallas Mavericks signed veteran Dwight Powell to a one-year, non-guaranteed contract for the 2026-26 NBA season. However, the Mavs already have 15 standard contracts on their roster, and Powell has played a big role in their two preseason games in Macau thus far.

Those performances also earned the 25-year-old some choice praise from head coach Dusty May, per The Athletic's Christian Clark. May revealed exactly why he chose to hand over the majority of the backup center minutes to Powell, claiming that his impact goes beyond what he produces on the court.

"When you watch the game, it's fairly obvious his ability to connect and keep the group organized," he said. "When you look at the age of — especially our second unit — Segio and Max and all these young guys, it just gives us another pressure release and outlet. He generates great looks. He's a very smart veteran basketball player."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

While May has started the Mavericks No. 9 pick of the 2026 draft Morez Johnson Jr. at Center in the two preseason games thus far, Powell has received considerable minutes off the bench. He played 13 minutes in the first game against the Houston Rockets, adding one point and eight assists and one block.

In the second game against Houston, Powell earned 15 minutes, contributing three points, five rebounds and an assist for his team. However, as May pointed out, his presence also proves to be a positive for the younger players in the Mavs' roster.

"So there are a number of different components to the development of young players," he said. Putting him out there with guys who (he) is trying to assist them, make them better, screen well for them. It's just a decision where we felt like we are playing well with him on the floor. We're very, very comfortable."

Hence, it will be interesting to see whether Powell ends up joining the Mavericks roster for the upcoming season. Per The Stein Line, Powell has also reportedly waived his right to block trades, meaning Dallas could trade him between Dec. 25 and the Feb. 11 deadline if he secures the 15th roster spot. However, keeping him would require the Mavericks to make room, potentially by releasing Moussa Cissé, whose $2.2 million salary became fully guaranteed after Dallas retained him beyond Oct. 1, or by arranging a trade.

articles.summary: The Orlando Magic suffered a crushing seven-game playoff defeat to the Detroit Pistons last season, and Marc Stein of The Stein Line says their future will b...
articles.body:
The Orlando Magic suffered a crushing seven-game playoff defeat to the Detroit Pistons last season, and Marc Stein of The Stein Line says their future will be in the spotlight this season. Magic guard Anthony Black is unlikely to get a contract extension. The lack of one seems to be because Orlando is already committed to several of its key veteran rotational pieces.

"The Stein Line has been advised by sources briefed on the situation to classify an extension for Magic swingman Anthony Black as unlikely at this current juncture," Stein wrote. "Sources say that the sides have not engaged in any meaningful extension dialogue to date — not during the offseason or even since training camps began — because the Magic have concerns about the long-term financial obligations they have already stacked up by signing Jalen Suggs to a lucrative extension in addition to frontcourt stalwarts Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner and summer of 2025 marquee trade acquisition Desmond Bane."

Stein also reports that the Magic front office wants to bring the majority of the playoff roster back, which could pose issues for Black.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Orlando lead executive Jeff Weltman has largely taken a run-it-back approach with the roster, knowing deep down that keeping both Suggs and Black is challenging (to put it mildly) financially. The big offseason change: Installing Sean Sweeney as the new head coach. All of which means Black, barring a shift in the state of negotiations over the next week-plus, could well have to face restricted free agency next summer despite his rising stature."

In his report on players eligible for rookie-scale contract extensions last week, ClutchPoints senior NBA insider Brett Siegel foresaw that Orlando's payment obligations could complicate Black's extension talks.

"Franz Wagner, Paolo Banchero, Desmond Bane, and Jalen Suggs account for roughly $161 million in payroll for the 2027-28 season. Add Wendell Carter Jr.'s $19.5 million, and the Magic now have a payroll exceeding $180 million between their starting five.

Siegel also pointed to a way Black could ink an extension that could make both parties happy.

This makes things difficult for Black in terms of a new extension, but the team could very well look to extend him on a similar value to that of Carter, around 12% of the total cap. Doing so would reward Black long-term while also giving the Magic options to keep this core together if the organization is open to paying luxury taxes. It is definitely possible that the two sides wait until next offseason when Black is a restricted free agent to get a deal done, but it would be advantageous to lock him in long-term now."

articles.title: What we learned from the Jets' win over the Browns
articles.summary: Identifying three things we learned from the New York Jets' Week 5 win over the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
The New York Jets picked up a much-needed victory in Week 5 , defeating the Cleveland Browns 17-12. It was a dominant defensive performance by head coach Aaron Glenn's squad. The offense also did enough to outlast the Browns.

Jets Wire identified three things we learned from a Jets victory that ended a three-game losing streak .

Concerns were mentioned about New York Jets rookie EDGE, David Bailey who entered this contest on a cold streak. Well, those concerns were firmly put to rest. Bailey produced a career-high three sacks, and added seven tackles, four QB hits, and three TFLs to his defensive totals. He was downright dominant.

Jets fans hoped to see rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq enjoy a bounce-back performance after his goose egg in Week 4. That did not happen for the former Oregon standout. Sadiq caught just two passes and lost a fumble inside the five-yard line. He stayed down and exited the game with a potential concussion. Brutal.

Inside the dominant defensive performance

The Jets won this game on defense. They limited the Browns' offense to 198 yards, forced two turnovers, and eight punts. The Browns lost the time of possession battle and were 4-of-16 on third down (and 0-for-2 on fourth down). The defense provided every opportunity to win the game, and the Jets capitalized.

For the third straight game, Nnamdi Madubuike led the defensive line group in snaps played (53). Travis Jones exited the game late after getting shaken up and finished with 38 snaps. On the edge, Tavius Robinson (48 snaps) and Mike Green (367 snaps) led the way with Trey Hendrickson sidelined again. Ethan Burke received a good amount of playing time again as well as the fourth edge rusher.

Teddye Buchanan saw his snap count increase slightly for a third consecutive game at linebacker since returning from injury. Buchanan is cleary still playing third banana behind Roquan Smith (64 snaps) and Trenton Simpson (36 snaps), though. Simpson stuffed the sheet again with a tackle for loss, sack and quarterback hit along with seven total tackles.

Cornerbacks Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey, who was questionable to play with a calf injury, did not leave the field (64 snaps each). There was a big drop-off to the next corner, Chandler Rivers, whose playing time took a dip from the last few games. Rivers played 19 snaps and veteran Chidobe Awuzie was only on the field for two defensive plays.

Kyle Hamilton exited the game briefly with an injury but returned after four plays, in time to make the game-winning interception in overtime. Malaki Starks played all but two snaps on defense (62) and had a team-high 10 tackles with two tackles for loss. Notably, No. 3 safety Jaylinn Hawkins' snap share took a decrease, as he played just 38 snaps.

articles.title: VOTE for the Morris/Sussex Football Player of Week 6
articles.summary: After another fun week of the high school football season, it's time to look back on the best performances.
articles.body:
After another fun week of the high school football season, it's time to look back on the best performances.

Read about the players who stood out last week and let us know who you think should be the Morris/Sussex Player of the Week in the poll at the bottom of this page.

Nanakwasi Adutwum-Addae, Morristown Beard

The senior running back ran 25 times for 207 yards and four rushing touchdowns in a 36-13 win over previously unbeaten Montclair Kimberley on Oct. 10. It was the first four touchdown game in his career and the second game this season with 200 or more rushing yards. Adutwum-Addae also led the Crimson's defense with 11 tackles, including a sack.

The sophomore running back dashed for 264 yards and four touchdowns on 18 carries in a 38-14 win over Warren Hills on Oct. 9. Alvarado had a pair of 2-yard touchdown runs in the first half for a 17-7 halftime lead for the Gaels. Alvarado's 70-yard sprint to the end zone in the third quarter put the game out of reach and kept Roxbury undefeated in the SFC Liberty Blue.

The sophomore wide receiver caught six passes for 149 yards and two receiving touchdowns in a 38-20 win over West Milford on Oct. 9. Baginski began the scoring with a 2-yard touchdown run, followed with a 54-yard touchdown grab in the first quarter and adding a 23-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter. The victory clinches Montville's first division title since 2006.

The senior running back rushed 13 times for 67 yards and the only two touchdowns of the game in a 14-0 win over Verona on Oct. 10. Barlow's 1-yard touchdown run in the first quarter were the only points of the game until Barlow broke free for a 28-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to cement the game. Wallkill Valley improves to 7-0 for the first time in school history.

The junior quarterback rushed 13 times for 93 yards and three touchdowns in a 40-7 win over Morristown on Oct. 9. Leading 20-7 at the half, Castillo was the only player to score in the second half. Castillo had touchdown runs of 12 and 6 yards in the third quarter and a 3-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter for the Marauders' best offensive showing in a month.

The senior running back rushed for 217 yards and three touchdowns on 17 carries in a 27-17 win over Indian Hills on Oct. 9. Chaplain's 75-yard touchdown run in the first quarter gave the Bombers an early lead, followed by a 16-yard touchdown run for a 13-3 halftime advantage. Chaplain's 27-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter secured the win.

The senior wide receiver scored three total touchdowns in a 42-0 win over Jefferson on Oct. 9. Connolly began the scoring with a 26-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Connolly had five catches for 128 yards, including a 70-yard touchdown catch from Connor Consiglio in the second quarter. In the third quarter, Connolly returned an interception 30 yards for another touchdown. It's the first victory for Jefferson over Morris Catholic since 1979.

The senior running back ran for a career-high 338 yards and five rushing touchdowns in a 50-20 win over Hackettstown on Oct. 9. After Geisen's 4-yard touchdown run in the first quarter, Geisen unleashed in the second quarter with touchdown runs of 72, 74 and 65 yards. Geisen capped his memorable night with a 35-yard touchdown run in the third quarter as the Vikings reached the 50-point total for the third time in school history.

The senior quarterback completed 27 of 38 passes for 356 yards and four passing touchdowns in a 34-17 win over Mendham on Oct. 9. Hogan found Nick Lagunowich for two passing scores, inclduing a 33-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter. Hogan connected in the third quarter on touchdown passes to Owen Coletta for 48 yards and Milo Semioli for 16 yards to build the Cougars lead to 27-3. Hogan's second touchdown pass to Lagunowich for 35 yards in the fourth quarter completed a career-best day for Hogan.

The sophomore quarterback completed 5 of 7 passes for 204 yards and four passing touchdowns in a 56-0 win over Bergen Tech on Oct. 9. Velasquez connected with Osvaldo Ortiz on an 86-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter and followed it with another touchdown pass to Ortiz from 15 yards in the second quarter. Velasquez completed a 40-yard touchdown pass to Christopher McKenzie in the second quarter and then a 50-yard touchdown pass to Max Piechota in the third. The offensive output was the most by a Dover team since scoring 59 points in a win over Hanover Park in 1996.

The junior quarterback completed 9 of 13 passes for 254 yards and four touchdowns in a 35-6 win over Kittatinny. Young tossed touchdown passes to Hunter Wolfe from 35 and 50 yards in the first quarter for a 21-6 lead. Young's 66-yard touchdown pass to Reid Corino in the second quarter built a 35-6 halftime lead.

articles.title: Jermaine Eluemunor’s calf issue headlines list of Giants’ Week 5 injuries
articles.summary: Eluemunor, Colton Hood, Tyler Nubin all forced to leave Sunday’s game.
articles.body:
New York Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor is undergoing an MRI on his calf on Monday , after injuring it during Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Washington Commanders.

The veteran right tackle played 44 snaps before suffering the injury, and having to be helped off the field by teammates Aaron Stinnie and John Michael Schmitz.

Second-year player Marcus Mbow took over at right tackle, playing the final 45 offensive snaps. Pro Football Focus charged Mbow with two pressures allowed in 36 pass-blocking snaps. If Eluemunor misses time, rookie J.C. Davis would likely take over as the swing tackle. Davis has been inactive for all five games this season.

Cornerback Colton Hood suffered a concussion making a tackle on a kickoff late in the third quarter. How quickly he progresses through the league's concussion protocol will determine whether or not he will be available this Sunday against the New Orleans Saints.

Nubin suffered a neck injury in the fourth quarter when he was hit by Washington center Lucas Patrick while trying to help make a tackle.

More on all of these injuries as information becomes available.

articles.title: Ex-Port Vale & Gillingham captain Loft dies at 39
articles.summary: Former Port Vale and Gillingham captain Doug Loft dies at the age of 39, following a medical emergency.
articles.body:
Former Port Vale and Gillingham captain Doug Loft has died at the age of 39.

A statement from Gillingham said he died following a medical emergency at the weekend.

Loft played 196 times for Vale between 2009 and 2014, after signing from Brighton & Hove Albion, and went on to make 70 appearances for the Gills.

"He will be remembered fondly by everyone at the club, not only for his achievements on the pitch but for the commitment and leadership he showed throughout his time in Burslem," a Port Vale statement said .

"The thoughts and heartfelt condolences of everyone at Port Vale are with Doug's family, friends, former team-mates and all those who knew him, at this incredibly sad time.

"With the blessing of Doug's family, we have requested permission from the EFL for our players to wear black armbands and to hold a minute's silence ahead of kick off at this weekend's game against Chesterfield."

Loft emerged at non-League Hastings United and signed for Brighton in January 2006, just after his 20th birthday.

He played three times in the Championship, scoring once, and made 46 further appearances for the Seagulls in League One.

After joining Port Vale, Loft was named the club's player of the season for 2011-12, and was appointed captain, leading the club to promotion from League Two.

He was signed by Gillingham in 2014 and also made captain.

Loft spent two seasons in League One at Priestfield.

"Our thoughts and condolences are with Doug's wife Laura, their children Freya and Amelie, along with his friends and family at this very difficult time," the Gillingham statement said.

Loft also had spells at Colchester United, Shrewsbury Town, Dagenham & Redbridge, Billericay Town and Tonbridge Angels.

Doug Loft signed for Vale in 2009, joining manager Micky Adams, who had worked with him at Brighton.

In the five years he had at the club, he made 196 appearances, scoring 19 goals. He won the player of the year award in 2012, then was named club captain as the team went on to secure automatic promotion from League Two.

He left in 2014 to move back south with his family.

Adams says "no one could have been prouder to have captained the club", and says he did it with "enthusiasm and endeavour".

articles.title: Back-to-back wins vault Chase Briscoe back into title contention, but is it too little, too late?
articles.summary: (AP) — Chase Briscoe's hero in auto racing has always been Tony Stewart. 19 Toyota is hoping to replicate what “Smoke" accomplished in 2011 when he stunned t...
articles.body:
CONCORD, N.C. (AP) — Chase Briscoe's hero in auto racing has always been Tony Stewart.

Now, the driver of the No. 19 Toyota is hoping to replicate what "Smoke" accomplished in 2011 when he stunned the racing world by rallying to win the NASCAR Cup Series championship by winning five of 10 playoff races, including the season finale at Homestead to register one of the sport's biggest comebacks.

"He made a pretty unbelievable run, and hopefully we can do the same thing," Briscoe said of Stewart.

Briscoe is certainly giving it his best effort after winning back-to-back playoff races.

That included Sunday when he edged out Joe Gibbs Racing teammate Christopher Bell by .029 seconds to win the second closest race in Charlotte Motor Speedway's 66-year history.

He also won the previous week at Las Vegas.

The wins have vaulted Chase back into the "Chase."

Two weeks ago Briscoe was 123 points behind playoff points leader Kyle Larson. He's since trimmed that deficit to 65 with four races remaining before a champion is crowned.

Denny Hamlin, at 49 points back, and Bell, 51 back, also remain ahead of Briscoe heading into the stretch run.

Now it's just a matter of whether it's too little, too late for Briscoe.

"I think we are certainly in contention," Briscoe said. "We probably need to win another race or two, but we at least put ourselves in the ballgame. That's all you can ask for."

Briscoe lamented four laps in the playoffs which he said have cost him 75 points due to miscues.

But he added the focus is on next week when the circuit heads to Phoenix.

"We never know how it's going to look in four weeks from now but just have to go to the racetrack and keep winning races ultimately, and if we can do that, the points are going to be what they're going to be at the end," he said.

Briscoe's crew chief James Small is hoping to seize on the momentum from the two wins.

"I think we've got to step on their throats while we can," Small said. "I'm not going to let off the throttle pedal right now."

When asked if the mild-mannered Briscoe was the type to step on someone's throat, Small laughed and said, "Definitely not."

But then Small added, "When he puts his helmet on and he's silent, but he's like a silent assassin."

Briscoe got a chuckle when informed of Small's comments after the race.

"You can be a nice guy outside of the race car, but in the race car I think you have to be a killer," Briscoe said. "For us, that's the whole approach."

Briscoe is expected to continue his "ultra aggressive" approach next week.

"The only way you're going to cut into the gap is by winning races," Briscoe said. "If you just run second or third and Larson runs second or third with you, like you're not going to gain 65 points in four weeks. Yeah, just have to go win races and just have to be ultra aggressive truthfully and try to do everything we can in our power, and if it's enough, it'll be enough at the end."

Larson's crew chief Cliff Daniels told reporters that Sunday was a good reality check for his team that the season isn't over.

Larson finished sixth on Sunday, marking the first time he has finished outside of the top five in the postseason. Still, he was able to add nine points to his lead over the second place Hamlin.

But Briscoe is the driver that clearly has his attention.

"I won't feel comfortable until it's over," Larson said. "Obviously, Briscoe winning and having a good day; you can take big chunks out of (the lead) if you win. We're going to go to some tracks where others are really good coming up, so we just have to keep putting together days like (Sunday). We weren't the fastest, but we got good points."
